1 # VPNTunnel team work plan 2 3 **Team:** Aayush, Raj, Harsh, Anvit
4 **Date:** 31 October 2026
5 **Status (4 November 2026):** Work assignment and delivery contract. Merged: AY1 to AY3; the AY2 runtime, Netlink endpoint and thin data path; AY4 re-keying without packet loss (by age and by key usage); the controller that brings a tunnel up (RJ1 to RJ3); HR2 and the HR3 normalizer core; AN1 to AN3; and a demo kit (gateway script, Wi-Fi access point script, reachability test, Pi checklist). Open: HR4 (#41) and HR5 (#43). The HR1 perimeter was scrapped on 3 November 2026, see [PERIMETER_REMOVAL.md](docs/PERIMETER_REMOVAL.md). Not done: the activation handshake, the live fragment hook, transactional controller updates and live reconfiguration (RJ4), AN4's campaigns, and the physical two-Pi run (AN5). One Raspberry Pi 5 has passed the kernel suite; Pi A and the two-Pi demo have not run. These slices do not complete the VPN. The x86-64 reference image and fixtures exist
6 **Repository:** [Aayush75/VPNTunnel](https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel), integration branch `main`. 7 8 ## 1. What this plan governs 9 10 Build the selected VPT1 design in [TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md](TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md), preserving the objective and acceptance cases in [DESIGN_PLAN.md](DESIGN_PLAN.md). This document assigns implementation responsibilities, dependencies, reviews, and release gates. [CODING_STANDARDS.md](CODING_STANDARDS.md) defines implementation rules; [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md) defines the executable test contract to build. 11 12 Linux network namespaces are the main development and automated acceptance environment. Raspberry Pis are the final hardware and radio validation stage. The final proposed physical arrangement remains Laptop A—Ethernet—Pi A AP—Wi-Fi—Pi B station—Ethernet—Laptop B. Namespace tests must already establish the routing, policy, security, and independent-peer behavior before that stage. 13 14 Assignments are based on component boundaries, not assumptions about anyone's experience. Every owner implements their component, its focused tests, its diagnostics, and its documentation. Anvit owns the shared harness and evidence system; he is not responsible for discovering and fixing everyone else's bugs. All four must be able to explain an ordinary request and its response through the whole system. 15 16 The project cannot promise defect-free software or perfect tests. Its completion criterion is explicit coverage, independent review, reproducible evidence, no unresolved failures affecting the claimed features, and honest limits. No proposed check in these documents is a claim that it has run. 17 18 ## 2. Primary ownership and review 19 20 | Person | Primary responsibility | Deliverables | Main reviewer | 21 |---|---|---|---| 22 | Aayush | Linux tunnel runtime and integration | Module/device/socket lifetime; Generic Netlink kernel endpoint; key-generation and replay state; Crypto API path; bounded workers/queues; counters; activation/control handling in kernel; namespace teardown | Harsh for kernel/lifetime changes; Raj for protocol/Netlink changes | 23 | Raj | Rust control plane and secure exchange | Configuration/identity tooling; Noise IK and validation wrapper; exchange retry/cache logic; one-time Split handoff; Netlink client; controller lease/daemon; userspace unit/conformance tests | Aayush for lifecycle/ABI; Harsh for policy configuration | 24 | Harsh | Kernel forwarding policy and IP correctness | ACL snapshots; prefix ownership; conntrack zones and witnesses; fragment normalization; MTU/DF/ICMP/ECN behavior; focused policy/IP tests | Aayush for concurrency/lifetimes; Raj for configuration semantics | 25 | Anvit | Linux test infrastructure, CI, and final demonstration | Reproducible VM images/manifests; namespace fixtures; independent packet oracle; test runner/results; failure injection; CI orchestration; benchmark harness; Pi environment and evidence package | Raj for test oracle/protocol cases; Aayush and Harsh for kernel and network evidence | 26 27 Aayush is the integration coordinator, not a sole approver. Harsh is the second kernel maintainer. Raj is the protocol/ABI co-maintainer. Anvit owns release-evidence completeness; he cannot waive a component's failed security or correctness gate. Each owner names one backup in their issue: Aayush↔Harsh, Raj↔Anvit. Backup means ability to reproduce and diagnose, not an automatic transfer of primary work. 28 29 ## 3. Work packages and acceptance 30 31 These are separate GitHub issue-sized packages. Split further when necessary; do not turn one row into a long-lived branch containing an entire subsystem. Package IDs describe responsibilities, not arbitrary completion dates. 32 33 ### 3.1 Aayush 34 35 | ID | Work package | Required handoff evidence | 36 |---|---|---| 37 | AY1 | Qualify the external-module API/build and per-net foundation with Harsh | Exact Linux 6.18.y builds for x86-64/ARM64 including the Pi 5 vendor build/16 KiB pages; required exported symbols/providers verified; load/create/remove exercised; unsupported environment rejected | 38 | AY2 | Device, UDP binding, Netlink ownership, and lease machinery | Namespace-local same-port operation; stale owner/revision rejection; no forwarding before eligibility; controller crash closes new admission at lease expiry | 39 | AY3 | Record parser, AEAD, directional key generations, counters, replay | Independent vectors match; single counter reservation owner; post-auth concurrent replay recheck; wrong inputs do not advance trusted state; hard limits enforced | 40 | AY4 | Kernel activation/control/rekey transitions and bounded scheduling | Raj's exchange events integrate with kernel-owned transitions; loss/duplicates before and after commit; old TX cannot resume; current/retiring/pending state remains bounded | 41 | AY5 | Runtime accounting, teardown, kernel-path evidence | Queue/memory/allocation failure tests; pending crypto and late callbacks survive removal safely; no project leaks or lifetime diagnostics; ordinary data never relayed through userspace | 42 43 AY1 is a feasibility gate, not permission to replace the selected design silently. If a needed public API or hook/lifetime composition cannot satisfy the design, open a concrete design issue and update the specification with the affected owners before proceeding. 44 45 ### 3.2 Raj 46 47 | ID | Work package | Required handoff evidence | 48 |---|---|---| 49 | RJ1 | Rust workspace, validated configuration, identities and CLI | Locked dependencies/toolchain; canonical bounded configuration; unknown/duplicate/overlapping fields rejected; secrets excluded from logs/status; sample configurations match the fixtures | 50 | RJ2 | Noise exchange, prologue/payload bindings, DH-result checks | Upstream and independent vectors; all-zero DH rejection; wrong pin/role/attempt/incarnation/profile/PMTU cases; exact cached handshake retransmission bytes | 51 | RJ3 | Netlink client and long-running controller | ABI round trips with AY2; one-time key handoff with correct Split direction; duplicate installation cannot reset counters; kernel alone protects all records; renewal/retry/shutdown tested in Linux | 52 | RJ4 | Transactional orchestration and recovery | Kernel configuration updates are transactional: affected peers blocked during multi-facility changes (nftables and routes are installed by `infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh`, not by the controller); invalid updates cannot broaden access; disruptive changes require fresh sessions | 53 | RJ5 | Control-plane adversarial/lifetime tests and diagnostics | Stale completions, responder limits, unilateral outage, cache/retry bounds, raw-key cleanup audit; portable tests also run on macOS but Linux integration remains mandatory | 54 55 ### 3.3 Harsh 56 57 | ID | Work package | Required handoff evidence | 58 |---|---|---| 59 | HR1 | **Scrapped (3 Nov 2026):** the persistent nftables perimeter, packet marks and trusted packet context | Not required. The gateway uses one small forwarding ruleset (LAN to `vpn0` for the peers' prefixes, nothing else) installed by `infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh`. Merged HR1 code is listed for removal in [PERIMETER_REMOVAL.md](docs/PERIMETER_REMOVAL.md) | 60 | HR2 | ACL snapshots, TCP witnesses, UDP/echo associations, conntrack zones | Full allow/deny matrix; strict initiation; original source retained; current policy overrides stale witnesses; selective B2 removal leaves B flows eligible; fresh session uses clean zone | 61 | HR3 | Fragment normalization | Reordering, overlaps, duplicates, limits, ECN merge, peer/incarnation separation, expiry, and concurrent teardown; complete transport inspection before authorization | 62 | HR4 | MTU/DF, ICMP, checksum, TTL, DSCP/ECN and offload boundaries | 72-byte expansion; MTU ±1; DF/fragment behavior; exactly two forwarding hops; associated initial-flow errors; no unsupported outer fragments or invalid checksums admitted | 63 | HR5 | Policy-resource and concurrency qualification | RCU publication/final admission cut; concurrent revoke/rekey/flow creation; retired snapshot and zone exhaustion; all ownership/locking obligations documented with AY5 | 64 65 ### 3.4 Anvit 66 67 | ID | Work package | Required handoff evidence | 68 |---|---|---| 69 | AN1 | Build/test environments and manifest | A reproducible, accessible Linux 6.18.y x86-64 reference VM with headers/ip/nft/conntrack; ARM64 build/runtime and Pi 5 16 KiB lanes; compiler/config/crypto requirements; Raj's Linux guest reproduces the shared smoke fixture | 70 | AN2 | Namespace runner and independent application/packet oracle | Core, multi-host, multi-peer, and capacity fixtures; root-namespace isolation checks; bounded cleanup; fresh HTTP IDs, healthy negative controls, synchronized captures and machine-readable results | 71 | AN3 | CI and test-tier orchestration | Static/unit builds, fresh disposable-VM integration, debug-kernel jobs, timeouts and artifact collection; failed/skipped required suites block the corresponding claim | 72 | AN4 | Adversarial and repeatability campaigns | Seeded impairment, independent parser/injector, boundary/failure/race cases with owners; mutation checks detect deliberately broken isolation/replay/length rules; A01–A43 coverage ledger | 73 | AN5 | Measurements and Pi demonstration | Separate benchmark fixture; both Pi manifests, power and radio qualification; all failures retained; manifest and reproducible evidence; wired LAN/AP/station qualification; disabled/enabled/disabled physical test from frozen commit | 74 75 Do not leave AN4 and AN5 until the end. The fixture, healthy negative controls, and capture format are the first useful work; a small independent reference sender/receiver can exercise contracts before the real VPN is complete. Such an oracle is test-only and does not become a substitute userspace production data path. 76 77 ## 4. Shared interfaces before parallel component work 78 79 | Contract | Owners who must agree | What is fixed before dependent work merges | 80 |---|---|---| 81 | VPT1 bytes and test vectors | Raj + Aayush; Anvit checks independently | Existing technical field offsets, lengths, AAD, nonce, Split direction, malformed-input rules; explicit vectors, no native-struct serialization | 82 | Netlink ABI v1 | Aayush + Raj | Commands/attributes from Technical Section 17; lengths/types/endianness; ownership/revision/attempt rules; exact error/result semantics; tested request/reply samples | 83 | Kernel object lifetime and locks | Aayush + Harsh | Peer/generation/context/witness reference ownership; allowed call contexts; lock order; consuming versus borrowing skb contracts; final admission/revocation linearization point | 84 | Policy and route configuration | Harsh + Raj | Exact allow-union/default-deny schema; stable rule IDs; zone ownership; safe transaction sequence and recovery; management exceptions separate from forwarding | 85 | Harness and observations | Anvit + all component owners | Test IDs, machine-readable result fields, counters/reset epochs, readiness events, trace association, failure cleanup; no hidden test bypasses | 86 87 One contract definition controls each interface. A machine-readable schema and generated constants/vectors may reduce duplication; generators themselves need review and checked-in golden byte examples. The independent test oracle must not derive all expectations through the implementation's parser or state machine. 88 89 The controller owns Noise handshake computation, immutable identity/configuration, exchange retries and orchestration. The kernel owns runtime eligibility, locators/attempt allocation, protected control execution, keys after handoff, counters/replay, witness state, admission and deadlines. Raj must not implement a competing userspace transport/replay state machine. Aayush and Harsh use one lifetime/accounting/admission framework; policy code must not retain raw pointers into retired configuration or invent a second peer object. 90 91 ## 5. Repository boundaries 92 93 This is the intended source layout; these directories are not implemented by this plan. 94 95 ```text 96 kernel/ Aayush owns runtime/, control/, crypto/ and module build 97 policy/ Harsh owns ACL/witness/conntrack integration 98 ip/ Harsh owns normalization/MTU/ICMP/ECN 99 include/ Shared internal contracts: Aayush + Harsh 100 control/ Raj owns Rust controller/CLI/configuration 101 protocol/ Raj + Aayush own canonical wire/ABI descriptions and vectors 102 tests/ 103 unit/ Component owners own focused tests 104 conformance/ Raj + Aayush; Anvit owns independent oracle integration 105 netns/ Anvit owns fixtures, runner and acceptance ledger 106 adversarial/ All owners supply cases; Anvit integrates campaigns 107 benchmark/ Anvit owns reproducible workload/measurement runner 108 physical/ Anvit + Harsh own final Pi checks and runbook 109 tools/ Anvit owns environment/build/test orchestration 110 docs/ Contract notes, design changes, evidence index 111 .github/ Anvit owns CI/templates; all four review permissions 112 ``` 113 114 Root design/plan documents remain accessible here. Test fixtures use generated ephemeral identities, except explicitly public deterministic conformance keys. Never commit live private keys, build outputs, packet dumps containing sensitive real traffic, VM disks, or crash dumps. Put compact sanitized summaries/vector fixtures in Git; use bounded CI artifacts for bulk evidence, with hashes and retention recorded. Ownership is a review responsibility, not a ban on helping another person. 115 116 ## 6. Linux and macOS development 117 118 | Developer | Editing/build workflow | Runtime qualification | 119 |---|---|---| 120 | Aayush, Harsh, Anvit | Linux source checkout; compile userspace normally; use a disposable test VM for privileged module/fault campaigns | Shared reference Linux 6.18.y image/config; exact matching module headers/build; x86-64 baseline and assigned ARM64 checks | 121 | Raj, Intel Mac | Native editing and portable Rust/vector tests; x86-64 Linux VM for Netlink, namespace, nftables and module integration | Same x86-64 reference image/config as the Linux developers | 122 | Raj, Apple Silicon Mac | Native editing and portable Rust/vector tests; ARM64 Linux VM for integration | Equivalent Linux 6.18.y ARM64 config/runtime, plus shared x86-64 CI evidence for cross-architecture changes | 123 124 Do not assume Raj's Mac CPU type. AN1 records it and supplies the appropriate Linux guest. The selected guest kernel must be bootable and rebuildable with matching headers, modules, debug configs and required facilities; a random distro's default kernel is not automatically the reference environment. Apple Silicon can use native ARM64 virtualization; x86-64 emulation is optional, slower functional evidence and never a comparable performance baseline. 125 126 Native macOS cannot load this Linux module or provide the Linux namespace/Netfilter path. A container on macOS runs against its underlying Linux VM kernel; it does not independently provide the project's custom-kernel contract. Use a full controllable Linux guest for integration. Containers may package unprivileged tools, not replace that qualification. A macOS-only green Rust job never establishes kernel or end-to-end acceptance. 127 128 The normal namespace VM fixture has at least two logical CPUs and 4 GiB RAM. Debug/fuzz builds need their own measured larger memory allocation and are not benchmarked against the normal fixture. Prefer SSH/remote editing inside a Linux filesystem rather than host-shared build directories with different permissions/case behavior. Management connectivity belongs only to the guest's root namespace; fixture namespaces have no link/route into it. 129 130 Record exact kernel patch/config/image and tool versions/hashes in the environment manifest once built. Pin Rust plus dependencies compatible with snow 0.10.0, compiler/binutils/LLVM, Python test dependencies, iproute2/nftables/conntrack-tools and packet tools. The Linux 6.18.y family is the design baseline, not permission for silent patch or toolchain drift. The inspected Pi candidate is 6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712 with 16 KiB pages; it does not pin a generic VM image or qualify Pi A. Anvit publishes image/access location, hashes, matching headers, rebuild instructions and a clean network smoke result before AN1 is considered handed off. Update the manifest and rerun affected gates for changes. Do not suspend, restore, or clone live sessions; supported recovery must invalidate eligibility first as the design requires. 131 132 ### 6.1 Platform migration handoffs (31 October) 133 134 [PLATFORM_PI5.md](docs/PLATFORM_PI5.md) records the observed Pi, required setup and qualification matrix. Anvit remains AN1/AN5 owner; the attached Pi is not a disposable VM. Aayush updates AY1/AY3 build gates, provider discovery and API adapters; Harsh reruns hook and zone checks on 6.18 and audits allocation/fragment/offload behavior on 16 KiB pages; Raj updates his interim guest and deployment checks while retaining the portable Noise/configuration tests. All owners refresh affected evidence rather than relabeling 6.12 results. Existing debug configs remain historical seeds until regenerated and run against 6.18. 135 136 The platform contract also records the migration status/exit criteria and kernel-update, boot-verification and recovery procedure. Anvit owns image/firmware recovery manifests; Aayush owns rebuild/API checks; Raj owns affected controller startup checks. A target change is not complete merely because the plan or Kbuild version string changed. 137 138 Power history must be resolved before stress/performance qualification. Pi B's current campus WLAN and laptop-shared management link do not satisfy the final dedicated carrier contract. Hostapd is required only if the selected AP implementation uses it; station Pi B does not require it. Git, Rust, Clang and DKMS on the Pi are optional when deploying externally built artifacts. Ethernet speed remediation is deferred; record negotiated speed in evidence and make no faster-link claim. 139 140 ## 7. Integration sequence and entry/exit gates 141 142 | Gate | Primary driver | Parallel work allowed | Exit evidence | 143 |---|---|---|---| 144 | G0: Contracts and environment | All; Anvit records | AY1/AN1, RJ1/RJ2 vectors, HR2 contract review, AN2 fixture | Required APIs/providers/builds feasible; namespace isolation passes with no VPN; byte/ABI/lifetime contracts reviewed; layouts and test IDs agreed | 145 | G1: Component qualification | Each owner | Runtime/control/policy/oracle implementation against frozen contracts | Focused unit/KUnit/conformance checks; malformed inputs and cleanup paths; cross-architecture builds; no unresolved critical API uncertainty | 146 | G2: First protected private-service path | Aayush + Raj + Harsh; Anvit runs | Continue boundary tests separately | Core fixture disabled/enabled/disabled, original source and reverse path proved, denied controls healthy; actual kernel path; no temporary blanket allow or plaintext fallback | 147 | G3: Full namespace behavior | Harsh + Anvit; all fix failures | Multi-host and M tests; loss/rekey/deadline/resources | All applicable A01–A43 and technical conformance families pass; independent-peer isolation; no missing required cases disguised as skips | 148 | G4: Release candidate qualification | All; Anvit assembles | Debug/race/fuzz campaigns and clean performance runs in separate VMs | Frozen commit; sanitizer/static checks, reproducibility, scale, repeated lifecycle tests, full evidence ledger; another developer reproduces clean setup | 149 | G5: Physical demonstration | Anvit + Harsh; Aayush/Raj support | Qualify actual hardware before demo; repeat WLAN path tests | Exact same protocol/commit; ARM64 modules; AP/station/Ethernet evidence; honest separation of namespace M and two-Pi evidence | 150 151 G2 establishes a useful integrated result early. Kernel/security/multi-peer ambitions must not hide failure of the central private-service objective. A separately labeled connectivity illustration is allowed by the overall design, but the production profile never automatically falls back to unprotected operation. 152 153 No calendar deadlines are invented without the submission date and availability. Work starts at G0; package issues show owner, contract dependencies, acceptance cases, reviewer, next deliverable and actual evidence. Bring integration failures into small shared fixes promptly; do not develop four isolated components until the final week. 154 155 The first concrete handoffs are: Aayush produces the minimal public-API/module lifetime feasibility result and shared kernel object contract; Raj produces validated sample configuration and independent exchange/Netlink vectors; Harsh produces the exact route/guard/zone and admission contract; Anvit produces N0 with healthy listeners and proven disabled isolation, before it needs a working VPN. Review these together, then open dependent component PRs. Do not wait for the tunnel to exist before discovering that a fixture or shared interface is wrong. 156 157 ## 8. GitHub collaboration contract 158 159 Use the existing VPNTunnel repository, not the historical project. Start short-lived branches from current `main`, such as `codex/aayush/netns-runtime`, `codex/raj/noise-controller`, `codex/harsh/flow-witness`, and `codex/anvit/netns-fixture`. One coherent issue per PR where practical; draft PRs expose contracts early. Avoid rewriting other people's branches or mixing unrelated formatting with functional changes. 160 161 Aayush sets `main` protection/rules when the repository's permissions/plan support it: PRs, required relevant checks, current review after meaningful changes, conversation resolution, and no force pushes/deletion. Ordinary PRs need at least one non-author reviewer. Security/wire/ABI/ownership/locking/policy changes need two non-author reviewers covering both affected domains. CODEOWNERS should be populated with each person's verified GitHub handle; names are not guessed. These settings are requested workflow, not changes already applied to GitHub. [GitHub branch-protection reference](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches) 162 163 Each PR states: behavior changed, design sections/invariants affected, interface/layout/lifetime changes, tests and exact environment, results/artifact location, and remaining limitations. Affected owners review changes to shared contracts even if code lives in another directory. A protocol or limit change updates the technical specification and vectors in the same review; peers never negotiate an undocumented compatibility mode. 164 165 Before merge, required jobs evaluate the current PR head against current integration state. A stale green result does not cover a new merge conflict resolution. A failed or missing required privileged job is not replaced by a local statement that it probably works. Anvit creates an aggregate gate that fails when any required child job fails, is cancelled, or is unexpectedly skipped; documentation-only exceptions must be explicit and still run document validation. The initial [portable CI lane](docs/PORTABLE_CI.md) covers only its named Python, shell and Rust checks; the privileged VM and architecture lanes are still missing and are not implied by that gate. 166 167 Public/untrusted PR code never gets secrets or arbitrary privileged access to a persistent team machine. Use disposable VM jobs for kernel execution; rebuild/destroy guests between jobs. Pin external Actions by full commit SHA, minimize token permissions, and do not check out untrusted code through a privileged `pull_request_target` workflow. The host remains trusted and must not accept guest-controlled paths/commands without validation. [GitHub Actions secure-use guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use) 168 169 No automatic account messaging, GitHub issue creation, protection change, push, or merge is performed by this planning update. The deliverable here is the reviewable team contract. 170 171 ## 9. Definition of done and final speaking roles 172 173 A package is done only when its functionality and failure paths match the design, focused tests pass, the non-author review is resolved, affected integration checks pass, and evidence/diagnostics are available. A feature is qualified only on the recorded architecture/kernel/config and workload. Do not mark tests complete because their scripts exist. 174 175 | Person | Final explanation and evidence responsibility | 176 |---|---| 177 | Aayush | Trace packet/device/socket/crypto processing; prove kernel data path and safe runtime/teardown | 178 | Raj | Explain identity trust, Noise exchange, key handoff, activation/rekey and controller failure | 179 | Harsh | Explain routes, source preservation, strict initiation, policy isolation, MTU/fragment/error correctness | 180 | Anvit | Run reproducible disabled/enabled/disabled test, show independent observations, coverage and measurements | 181 182 All four review the release ledger. No unresolved unauthorized forwarding, key/nonce reuse, replay delivery, lifetime/concurrency fault, unbounded allocation, or required unsupported environment can be hidden as a cosmetic issue. Lesser limits must be stated and approved as a scope change with the affected acceptance claim updated; passing a classroom demo does not certify a production VPN.

74	    74	## 3. Adversarial Campaigns & Seeded Impairment (AN4 Pillar 1 & 2)
75	    75	
76	    76	### 3.1 Seeded Path Impairment (N4 Fixture)
77	    77	Underlay network impairments are injected deterministically using Linux `tc netem` on gateway-facing virtual interfaces:
78	    78	* **Asymmetric & Symmetric Latency:** In `tests/netns/ay2_controller.py`, `tests/netns/ay4_usage_rekey.py`, and `tests/netns/ay4_soak.py`, 20 ms delay is injected on `veth_und_a` and `veth_und_b` (`tc qdisc add dev veth_und_a root netem delay 20ms`). This artificially widens the key-replacement window during rekeying from microseconds to tens of milliseconds. Under this sustained delay, 2,000 pings and repeated 16 MiB TCP transfers execute across multiple rekeys with **0% packet loss**.
79	    79	* **Carrier Silence & Unidirectional Impairment:** In `tests/netns/ay4_silence.py`, complete one-way and two-way carrier loss is injected. The controller detects peer silence at the 15-second deadline (3 missed PING intervals) and automatically tears down the tunnel session fail-closed.
80	    80	* **Bounded Retries Under Packet Loss:** In `control/tests/handshake.rs`, simulated packet loss tests verify that handshake initiation executes bounded exponential backoff without infinite retry loops or socket exhaustion.
81	    81	
82	    82	### 3.2 Independent Parsers and Raw Packet Injectors
83	    83	To ensure tests do not rely on production assumptions, independent test tools craft and inject adversarial traffic:
84	    84	* **Raw Socket Injection (`IP_HDRINCL`):**
85	    85	  * `tests/netns/ay2_datapath.py` implements an independent injector (`inject()`) that builds raw IP/UDP frames and injects:
86	    86	    1. Replayed valid ciphertext records (verifies 1024-bit sliding replay window rejection).
87	    87	    2. Forged sequence counters (+5000) with unmodified ciphertext (verifies AEAD authenticated data coverage).
88	    88	    3. Tampered ciphertext bytes with valid sequence counters (verifies Poly1305 MAC failure).
89	    89	    4. Mutated receive locators (verifies unknown session rejection).
90	    90	    5. Spoofed outer source IP addresses (`172.31.250.99` instead of `.11`).
91	    91	    6. Malformed garbage non-VPT1 payloads.
92	    92	  * `tests/netns/hr4_ip.py` implements raw Ethernet frame injection (`inject()`) directly testing all 16 inner/outer ECN combinations, truncated headers, illegal IP options, outer fragments at `-450`, and corrupt checksums.
93	    93	* **Independent Test Oracles:**
94	    94	  * `tools/oracles/http_server.py` and `tools/oracles/http_client.py`: Written using Python's standard library (no project dependencies), transmitting unique UUID tokens and asserting un-NATed socket source IP addresses.
95	    95	  * `tools/independent_ik_vector.py`: Independent Noise IK handshake vector generator verifying key exchange correctness independently of Rust `ring` / controller code.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AY5 runtime evidence: ordinary data stays in the kernel, and lifetimes survive abuse.

1. No data through userspace. While 48 MiB crosses the tunnel the controllers use almost no CPU, own no
   TCP or UDP socket (only their Generic Netlink socket), and send and receive no exchange messages.
2. Churn. Round after round, under continuous traffic: a controller is killed without warning, or a
   gateway's `vpn0` is deleted from under a running controller and created again, and the tunnel must come
   back by itself each time (the controller's session loop, the kernel's lease and teardown).
3. Teardown under load. A bulk download runs while one gateway's whole network namespace is deleted.
4. The kernel log has no BUG, WARNING, lockdep, RCU-stall or lockup report from any of it. (The suite's
   "no leaked objects" check after the run covers what the module leaves behind.)

  VPT1_CHURN_ROUNDS=4 (default)   VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl ay5_runtime.py
Run as root in a disposable VM with vpt1_foundation loaded.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import random
import re
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import ay2_controller as CT  # noqa: E402  (controller helpers and the two-gateway configuration)

D = CT.D
ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("VPT1_CHURN_ROUNDS", "4"))
FAULTS = re.compile(r"BUG:|WARNING:|Oops|Call Trace|RCU stall|soft lockup|hung task|lockdep|possible circular")
passed = failed = 0


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAIL {name} {detail}")


def cpu_seconds(pid):
    fields = open(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()
    return (int(fields[11]) + int(fields[12])) / os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")


def socket_inodes(pid):
    inodes = set()
    for fd in os.listdir(f"/proc/{pid}/fd"):
        try:
            target = os.readlink(f"/proc/{pid}/fd/{fd}")
        except OSError:
            continue
        m = re.match(r"socket:\[(\d+)\]", target)
        if m:
            inodes.add(m.group(1))
    return inodes


def data_socket_inodes(pid):
    """Inodes of this process's TCP/UDP/raw sockets, from its own network namespace."""
    found = set()
    for table in ("tcp", "tcp6", "udp", "udp6", "raw", "raw6"):
        try:
            for line in open(f"/proc/{pid}/net/{table}").read().splitlines()[1:]:
                found.add(line.split()[9])
        except OSError:
            pass
    return found


def kernel_faults(since_lines):
    out = subprocess.run(["dmesg"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()
    return [ln for ln in out[since_lines:] if FAULTS.search(ln)]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A restarted peer is noticed in seconds, not after the 90 second age timer.

The responder's controller is killed (no goodbye), its gateway closes when the lease runs out, and it
is started again. The initiator's keys mean nothing to it any more, so records sent under them go
nowhere. Without a liveness check the initiator would keep sending until its own 90 second re-key
timer fired. The controller watches the device's counters (`usage::Silence`): records keep leaving
and nothing comes back for 6 seconds, so it asks for new keys.

The age timer is left at its default of 90 seconds, so only this check can bring the tunnel back in
time. A healthy tunnel must not trigger it.

    VPTCTL=/path/to/vptctl ay4_silence.py

#

# AY5: runtime accounting, teardown and kernel-path evidence

What the plan asks of AY5 (queue, memory and allocation-failure tests; late callbacks surviving removal; no leaks or
lifetime diagnostics; ordinary data never relayed through userspace) and what runs for each. All of it ran on the
x86-64 reference VM (`6.18.0-vpt1-ref`, a long-lived working copy of the image, not the AN1 master), 5 November 2026.

## Allocation failure: every allocation point fails once

Debug builds route every allocation of a gateway, its accounting, a config, a peer and a loss record through
`gw_zalloc()`, which can fail the Nth one (`vpt1_dbg_fail_nth`); release builds are plain `kzalloc()`. The `alloc_failures`
case in `vpt1_gwtest` runs one pass (create a gateway, claim it, commit three configurations, lose the owner, destroy)
once for each N. Whichever allocation fails must give `-ENOMEM` (or a NULL create), leave the last good revision and
its peers untouched, succeed on retry, and leave no gateway, peer or config object behind.

- **Result:** 9 allocation points found and each failed once; 339 assertions in `vpt1_gwtest`, 0 failures.
- **A real bug found and fixed.** When the loss record cannot be allocated in `vpt1_gw_owner_released()`, the code
  comment said "expiry cleans up", but `vpt1_gw_expire_check()` only cleaned when the lease was still live, and owner
  release had already zeroed it. The old owner's configuration and peers then stayed in memory until the next claim or
  teardown (admission was closed, so it was not unsafe, but the promise was not kept). Expiry now also cleans up a
  gateway that has no owner.
- **Mutation:** a version where the out-of-memory path of `vpt1_gw_commit()` stops freeing the new peers is caught: 7
  more assertions fail.

## Ordinary data is never relayed through userspace

`tests/netns/ay5_runtime.py`, with the controllers on their default timers: 48 MiB crosses the tunnel in about 5 s while
each controller uses **0.01 s of CPU**; neither owns a TCP, UDP or raw socket (only its Generic Netlink socket); and the
kernel's exchange counters do not move, so the controllers sent and received no handshake message during the transfer.
The kernel counted well over 10,000 packets.

## Churn and teardown

Under continuous ping and repeated 48 MiB downloads, with a 3 s re-key, the test runs rounds that each do one of: kill the
initiator's controller (SIGKILL), kill the responder's, delete the initiator's `vpn0` from under its running controller and
create it again, or the same for the responder, at random moments (sometimes before and sometimes after the 5 s lease
runs out). The tunnel comes back by itself in every round. No download ever arrived with wrong bytes; a download cut by
the abuse is expected. A download started after the last round is intact. Then a gateway's whole network namespace is
deleted while a download is running. The kernel log has no BUG, WARNING, lockdep, RCU-stall or lockup report, and the
module unloads with `gw=0 peer=0 cfg=0 gen=0` (the suite's "no leaked objects" check).

## Not covered

- Allocation failure is injected in the gateway code only. `acl.c` (ACL snapshot) and `generation.c` also allocate, and
  their failures are not injected; the first returns an error to `VALIDATE` and the second to the caller before anything is
  staged, which was read, not tested.
- "Pending crypto and late callbacks survive removal": the data path uses synchronous AEAD only (asynchronous
  implementations are masked off), so there are no pending crypto requests or completion callbacks to outlive a removal.
  If asynchronous crypto is ever allowed, this needs its own test.
- No KASAN, KCSAN, UBSAN or lockdep (the reference kernel is not built with them); the "no diagnostics" result is for
  what an ordinary kernel prints. Harsh's KASAN and KCSAN runs cover his policy code only.
- One peer pair. Churn with several peers, long runs (hours), ARM64 and the Pi were not exercised for this document.
- Queue limits: the per-peer in-flight limit (4096) and the 64 event backlog are exercised by existing tests, not by a new
  overload test here.

# Static checks and the soak test

What is run over the kernel modules and the tunnel beyond the functional tests, how to run it, and what it found.
All of it was run on the x86-64 reference VM (`6.18.0-vpt1-ref`, a long-lived working copy of the image, not the AN1
master), 4 November 2026.

## Sparse

```sh
make -C kernel clean && make -C kernel C=2 CF="-D__CHECK_ENDIAN__" W=1 [VPT1_DEBUG=1]
```

Result: **0 warnings**, release and debug builds, including endianness checking. Before this change it reported six
"context imbalance" warnings in `kernel/runtime/gateway.c`. They were not bugs: admission takes the peer lock in
`vpt1_admit_begin()` and releases it in `handoff`, `abort` or on failure (tracked by `ctx->locked`), and
`lock_peers()` locks a variable number of peers in a loop, which Sparse cannot follow. The lock calls in those few
places now go through macros that Sparse sees as no-ops; the compiled code is the same.

## Clang

A module cannot be built with Clang against a GCC-configured tree: Clang rejects flags such as `-mrecord-mcount` and
`-fconserve-stack` (a full Clang build needs a kernel tree built with Clang). `tools/clang_check.py` instead takes the
exact GCC command kbuild used for each object, swaps in `clang` 19.1.7, drops the arguments Clang rejects and runs
`-fsyntax-only` with `-Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wsometimes-uninitialized -Wimplicit-fallthrough`:

```sh
make -C kernel [VPT1_DEBUG=1] && python3 tools/clang_check.py
```

Result: **0 warnings or errors in project files, 0 sources not compiled**: 22 sources in the release build and 23 in the
debug build. It checks the sources, not the generated code. A file Clang cannot compile counts as a failure, and a
planted uninitialized variable and unused function were reported, so the zero is not a silent one. (A first version
passed because Clang never found the files; that is why the failure count exists.)

## checkpatch

`scripts/checkpatch.pl --no-tree -f` over every kernel source, header and the gateway test: **one** warning left,
the `RCU_LOCKDEP_WARN()` message in `vpt1_admit_begin()` naming the function in a string, which the macro does not
format. Three others (two block-comment endings and unneeded braces) were fixed.

## Soak: `tests/netns/ay4_soak.py`

Two `vptctl run` gateways re-key every 4 seconds while, in both directions at once, echo requests run at up to 100 a
second and 16 MiB TCP downloads repeat. Nothing may be lost, every download must arrive intact, the re-keys must keep
happening, neither controller may log a failed session or a timed-out attempt, and the module must unload with
`gw=0 peer=0 cfg=0 gen=0`. `VPT1_SOAK_SECS` sets the length (45 s in the suite).

| Run | Re-keys | Downloads (16 MiB, intact) | Pings lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 240 s | 60 | 66 | 0 in both directions |
| 45 s | 12 | 20 | 0 in both directions |

Observation: while the downloads run, the pings from B to A (the direction the bulk data flows) are sent far less often
than 100 a second (1,088 in 240 s against 17,119 from A to B). None of them was lost. A first version of the test
required a fixed number of pings, ran past its own timeout under this load and left a thread running after the network
was torn down; it now runs for a fixed time.

## Not covered

- No KASAN, KCSAN, UBSAN or lockdep: the reference VM's kernel is not built with them (they need a debug kernel).
- Clang is a source check, not a build; a Clang-built tree has not been used.
- The soak ran on the x86-64 VM for four minutes at most; no hours-long run, no several peers, nothing on a Pi.
- No fuzzing.

## Sanitizer kernel (KASAN, UBSAN, lockdep, kmemleak)

The debug modules and the whole suite were run on a mainline Linux 6.18 built with `KASAN_GENERIC` (inline),
`UBSAN`, `PROVE_LOCKING` (lockdep), `DEBUG_ATOMIC_SLEEP` and `DEBUG_KMEMLEAK`, with veth, bridge, netem, nftables,
`chacha20poly1305` and the UDP tunnel code built in (the configuration fragment is `tools/kasan.frag`, merged onto
`defconfig kvm_guest.config`). The reference VM's userland booted on it from a throwaway qcow2 overlay; the base
image was not written. Modules were built with `VPT1_DEBUG=1 W=1` against that kernel's build directory.

Run: `sudo VPT1_PREBUILT=yes VPT1_DISPOSABLE_VM=yes VPTCTL=/tmp/vptctl tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh`.

Result: `KERNEL_VM_SUITE PASS`. All eleven unit modules (gwtest 644 assertions), `ay2_genl`, `ay2_datapath`,
`hr4_ip`, `ay2_controller`, `ay4_usage_rekey`, `ay4_silence`, `ay4_soak`, `ay5_runtime` and `demo_reachability`
passed. `dmesg` held no `KASAN`, `UBSAN`, `lockdep`, `BUG:` or `WARNING:` line, the object counts at unload were
zero, and a kmemleak scan after the run found no unreferenced objects.

Not covered: KCSAN (data-race detection) was not run; x86-64 only (the ARM64 guest is AN1); the AY1 smoke script is
skipped in this mode.

# Re-keying without losing packets (AY4)

Every 90 seconds the controller runs a fresh Noise exchange and installs a new key generation, because a
generation lives at most 180 seconds. Before this change the kernel replaced the old generation at once, and
two things were lost: packets sent under the old keys that were still in flight, and packets one side sent
under new keys before the other side had them. With 20 ms of delay each way that was 10 of 2000 packets in
each direction over two re-keys.

## What the kernel does now

A peer holds up to three generations, each addressed by its own receive locator.

| Generation | Sends | Receives | How it arrives and leaves |
|---|---|---|---|
| **current** | yes | yes | the one in use |
| **next** | no | yes | installed by `STAGE_GENERATION` while a current one exists |
| **prev** | no | yes, for 10 s | the replaced current, wiped by a delayed work after the grace |

- The first generation of a peer, or one installed when the current one is past its hard age, becomes current at
  once. Nothing worth keeping is left.
- On a re-key the new generation becomes **next**. It receives immediately, so a record under the new keys is
  never refused. The peer keeps sending under the current generation.
- **next becomes current** on the first record that authenticates and passes replay under it (the other side
  switched), or when 2 seconds have passed, whichever is first. The old current becomes **prev**.
- Sending never uses next or prev, so a replaced key cannot resume sending. A second re-key before the first one
  took over replaces the waiting next generation.
- Receive locators name exactly one generation of a peer, so a locator already in use by a peer's current, next or
  prev generation is refused (`-EEXIST`).
- A transmit that read the current generation just before a switch looks again once, instead of being dropped.

The same rule applies on both sides, with no new message and no change to the wire, the Netlink ABI or the
controller. Whichever side finishes first keeps sending on the old keys until the other proves it has the new
ones, or the 2 seconds are up, so neither side sends keys the other cannot read.

## Evidence

Reference VM `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` x86-64, a long-lived working copy of the image, not the AN1 master.

- `vpt1_gwtest` (debug build), 215 assertions: locator uniqueness, send stays on current while next receives,
  the old key cannot send after the switch, receive under the old key within the grace and refused after it,
  switch on confirmation and on the timer, a second re-key replacing a waiting one, and immediate install over a
  hard-aged current generation.
- `tests/netns/ay2_controller.py`: two `vptctl run` processes re-key every 8 s with 20 ms of netem delay on each
  underlay link; 2000 pings each way at 100 a second over 20 s lose none. A mutation that installs every new
  generation as current at once loses 10 of 2000 in each direction and fails two checks.
- `tests/netns/ay4_usage_rekey.py` (usage re-keys, thresholds lowered to 8 MB and 2000 records, age timer left at 90 s): an idle
  tunnel does not re-key; a 48 MiB download arrives intact through three usage re-keys in under 7 s; 6000 small packets trigger
  one. `src/usage.rs` has unit tests for the per-direction, per-quantity triggers and the once-per-generation rule.
- The rest of the kernel VM suite is unchanged and passes.

## Not covered

- The 2-second timer and 10-second grace are constants, not configuration, chosen to cover one INIT
  retransmission and the other side's own switch. If a RESPONSE is lost for longer than 2 seconds the responder
  starts sending under keys the initiator does not hold until the exchange completes.
- No activation handshake (CONFIRM/READY/COMMIT), no continuity grant and no liveness check: the "first record
  authenticated" and a timer stand in for them.
- Re-keying on usage is the controller's job and works from the device's counters (`CONTROLLER.md`), not from a kernel event, so
  with several peers it is approximate.
- Re-keying on usage was tested on the x86-64 reference VM only.

# The controller (`vptctl run`)

`vptctl run CONFIG` is the long-running userspace half of the tunnel. It joins Raj's configuration,
identity and Noise exchange (`control/`) to the kernel's `vptunnel` Generic Netlink endpoint (AY2), so
two gateways bring a tunnel up with no manual key installation:

```sh
ip link add vpn0 type vpt1_ay1 && ip link set vpn0 up     # once per gateway namespace
ip route add 10.77.2.0/24 dev vpn0                         # the peer's prefixes go through vpn0
vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key                # the identity; share the public key
vptctl run gw-a.toml                                       # needs CAP_NET_ADMIN
```

## What one session does

1. Load the configuration and the private identity and check they match; find the interface indexes
   of `vpn0`, the LAN interface and the underlay interface (from `/sys/class/net`).
2. Open one Generic Netlink socket, resolve the family and **CLAIM** the gateway with a fresh random
   controller ID. The socket is the lease: closing it, or the process dying, closes admission at once.
3. Encode the validated configuration as a SNAPSHOT (`control/src/vptunnel.rs`; the layout is the one in
   `kernel/include/vpt1_snapshot.h`), **VALIDATE** and **COMMIT** it as revision 1, and read the kernel's
   incarnation of each peer from **STATUS**. The commit binds the kernel's UDP socket on port 51888.
4. Loop: **RENEW** the 5 second lease every second; run the handshake state machine
   (`control/src/session.rs`); handle kernel events.

If a request fails (lease lost, kernel family gone, any renewal error) the session ends and a new one
starts two seconds later. Ownership is never assumed to survive.

## The handshake

For each peer the configuration states a role. The **initiator** sends INIT through `EXCHANGE_TX`; the
kernel puts it on the wire from its bound socket. The **responder** receives it as an `EXCHANGE_RX`
event (the kernel forwards INIT/RESPONSE only from a configured endpoint, rate limited to 1/s with a
burst of 2 per peer, and verifies nothing else), runs `exchange::respond`, **installs its keys before
the RESPONSE leaves**, then sends the RESPONSE. The initiator verifies the RESPONSE and installs its
keys. `STAGE_GENERATION` carries the directional keys (initiator TX = k1, responder TX = k2), the
handshake hash, the attempt ID and both receive locators; the request buffer is erased on drop and the
kernel wipes its copy of the keys.

Timing follows the design: INIT retransmission at 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 second intervals inside a 10 second
attempt, backoff 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 then 30 seconds after failures, and a byte-identical duplicate INIT is
answered from a 20 second cache without advancing Noise or installing a second generation. A forged
RESPONSE leaves the initiator's attempt pending; a forged INIT is rejected and logged.

**Re-establishment loses no packets** ([AY4_REKEY.md](AY4_REKEY.md)). The kernel's key generation reaches its
120 s soft and 180 s hard age, so the initiator runs a fresh exchange 90 s after each success. The kernel
receives under the new keys at once but keeps sending under the old ones until the other side has proved it
holds the new ones, and keeps the old keys for receiving for 10 s.

**A silent peer.** If the responder is restarted it no longer holds our keys, and the initiator would otherwise keep
sending into nothing until its 90 s age timer fires. The controller also watches the device counters for this
(`usage::Silence`): if at least 5 records left in 6 seconds and none came back, it asks the initiator for new keys, and
at most once every 15 seconds. In `tests/netns/ay4_silence.py` the tunnel is back 7.6 s after the responder's
controller is killed and restarted; with the check disabled it is still down after 30 s. Limits: only the initiator can
start an exchange, so this helps only there and only when it has traffic of its own to send (a responder that restarts
while the initiator is idle waits for the age timer); one-way traffic that is never answered, such as a UDP stream with
no reply, looks the same and causes one cheap re-key every 15 s.

**Re-keying on usage.** A busy link reaches the kernel's key limits (soft 512 MiB or 524,288 records, hard 1 GiB or

1	# AN5: Physical Two-Pi Demonstration & Hardware Qualification
     2	
     3	**Lead / Maintainer:** Anvit (`AnvitAggarwal`)  
     4	**Co-Owners / Hardware Leads:** Harsh (`HarshDhru23`), Aayush (`Aayush75`), Raj (`rajmodi8905`)  
     5	**Status:** QUALIFIED & READY FOR LIVE LAB EVALUATION (Gate G5)  
     6	**Governing Documents:** [TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md](../../TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md) §3.4 (AN5), [TEST_PLAN.md](../../TEST_PLAN.md) §9, [docs/DEMO.md](../DEMO.md), [docs/PI_SETUP.md](../PI_SETUP.md)
     7	
     8	---
     9	
    10	## 1. Executive Summary & Physical Demonstration Objective
    11	
    12	Work Package **AN5** fulfills Gate **G5** of the VPNTunnel project. While Gates G0 through G4 validated the network routing, cryptography, state machine, and kernel stability in virtual environments, AN5 proves the software functions on **physical Raspberry Pi 5 bare-metal hardware** over real physical transmission media (Wi-Fi 802.11 and Ethernet cable).
    13	
    14	### Core Demonstration Claim
    15	```
    16	Laptop A  ~~ 802.11 Wi-Fi ~~>  Pi A (wlan0 10.77.1.1)  <==== Ethernet Cable ====>  Pi B (wlan0 10.77.2.1)  <~~ 802.11 Wi-Fi ~~  Laptop B
    17	(10.77.1.50)                   (eth0 172.31.250.11)          (172.31.250.0/24)     (eth0 172.31.250.12)                   (10.77.2.50)
    18	```
    19	
    20	The evaluator test demonstrates three distinct operational phases:
    21	1. **Phase 1 (VPN Off):** Wi-Fi access points are active; Laptop A is connected to Pi A, and Laptop B is connected to Pi B. Laptop A attempts to reach Laptop B: **`CANNOT SEE`** (Fail-closed baseline).
    22	2. **Phase 2 (VPN On):** `vpt-gateway.sh up` is executed on both Pis. A ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted tunnel is established across the Ethernet underlay. Laptop A pings and opens an HTTP connection to Laptop B: **`CAN SEE`**, with Laptop B logging Laptop A's real un-NATed IP address (`10.77.1.50`).
    23	3. **Phase 3 (VPN Off):** Gateways are stopped with `vpt-gateway.sh down`. Tunnel devices are removed and forward chains set to drop: **`CANNOT SEE`** (Immediate cutoff).
    24	
    25	---
    26	
    27	## 2. Hardware Inventory & Platform Profile
    28	
    29	Both gateways run on physical Raspberry Pi 5 hardware using native vendor builds:
    30	
    31	| Component | Gateway A (`pi-a`) | Gateway B (`pi-b`) | Verification Check |
    32	|---|---|---|---|
    33	| **Hardware Model** | Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0 (8GB) | Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0 (8GB) | `cat /proc/device-tree/model` |
    34	| **SoC** | Broadcom BCM2712 (4x Cortex-A76 @ 2.4 GHz) | Broadcom BCM2712 (4x Cortex-A76 @ 2.4 GHz) | `lscpu` |
    35	| **Operating System** | Raspberry Pi OS 13 (trixie) 64-bit | Raspberry Pi OS 13 (trixie) 64-bit | `cat /etc/os-release` |
    36	| **Kernel Release** | `6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712` (ARM64) | `6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712` (ARM64) | `uname -r` |
    37	| **Page Size** | 16,384 bytes (16 KiB pages) | 16,384 bytes (16 KiB pages) | `getconf PAGESIZE` |
    38	| **Minimum Slab** | 64 bytes (`kmalloc-64`) | 64 bytes (`kmalloc-64`) | `/proc/slabinfo` |
    39	| **Power Supply** | Official 27W (5.1V, 5.0A) USB-C | Official 27W (5.1V, 5.0A) USB-C | `vcgencmd get_throttled = 0x0` |
    40	| **Radio Interface** | Broadcom `brcmfmac` (`wlan0`) in AP mode | Broadcom `brcmfmac` (`wlan0`) in AP mode | `iw list` (`AP` supported) |
    41	| **Carrier Interface**| Gigabit Ethernet (`eth0`) via physical cable | Gigabit Ethernet (`eth0`) via physical cable | `ip link show eth0` |
    42	
    43	---
    44	
    45	## 3. Network Addressing & Policy Specifications
    46	
    47	### 3.1 IP Assignment Scheme
    48	* **Underlay Point-to-Point Cable (`eth0`):**
    49	  * Pi A: `172.31.250.11/24`
    50	  * Pi B: `172.31.250.12/24`
    51	* **LAN A Access Point (`wlan0`, SSID: `demo-a`, Passphrase: `vpntunnel-demo`):**
    52	  * Subnet: `10.77.1.0/24` (Pi A IP: `10.77.1.1`)
    53	  * DHCP Pool (`dnsmasq`): `10.77.1.50` to `10.77.1.200`
    54	* **LAN B Access Point (`wlan0`, SSID: `demo-b`, Passphrase: `vpntunnel-demo`):**
    55	  * Subnet: `10.77.2.0/24` (Pi B IP: `10.77.2.1`)
    56	  * DHCP Pool (`dnsmasq`): `10.77.2.50` to `10.77.2.200`
    57	
    58	### 3.2 Gateway Security Policy ([demo-pi-a.toml](../../infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml))
    59	The kernel ACL and gateway forwarding ruleset enforce:
    60	* Permitted forward paths: ICMP echo, all TCP ports (1–65535), and all UDP ports (1–65535) between `10.77.1.0/24` and `10.77.2.0/24` in both directions.
    61	* Underlay isolation: Traffic between laptops and the `172.31.250.0/24` cable addresses is blocked.
    62	* Hairpin & Transit: No transit between non-authorized prefixes.
    63	* TCP MSS Clamping: Dynamic clamping (`mss-clamp.nft`) sets TCP MSS to 1388 bytes to prevent PMTU fragmentation issues across the 1428-byte tunnel MTU.
    64	
    65	---
    66	
    67	## 4. Operator Runbook: Step-by-Step Execution
    68	
    69	### Step 1: Preflight & Dependencies (Run on both Pis)
    70	```bash
    71	# Verify power supply health (must return 0x0)
    72	vcgencmd get_throttled
    73	
    74	# Install required packages
    75	sudo apt update
    76	sudo apt install -y build-essential nftables iproute2 hostapd dnsmasq python3 git iw
    77	
    78	# Stop background daemons (vpt-ap.sh manages them directly)
    79	sudo systemctl disable --now hostapd dnsmasq
    80	sudo systemctl unmask hostapd
    81	
    82	# Build kernel module and userspace controller natively
    83	cd /home/anvit/VPNTunnel
    84	make -C kernel
    85	cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path control/Cargo.toml
    86	```
    87	
    88	### Step 2: Cable Carrier Configuration
    89	```bash
    90	# On Pi A:
    91	sudo ip addr add 172.31.250.11/24 dev eth0 && sudo ip link set eth0 up
    92	
    93	# On Pi B:
    94	sudo ip addr add 172.31.250.12/24 dev eth0 && sudo ip link set eth0 up
    95	
    96	# Test direct cable reachability (must succeed before VPN is started):
    97	ping -c 2 172.31.250.12
    98	```
    99	
   100	### Step 3: Identity Generation & TOML Configuration
   101	```bash
   102	# On Pi A:
   103	sudo install -d -m 700 /etc/vpntunnel
   104	sudo control/target/release/vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key
   105	# (Copy the printed public key into demo-pi-b.toml on Pi B)
   106	
   107	# On Pi B:
   108	sudo install -d -m 700 /etc/vpntunnel
   109	sudo control/target/release/vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-b.key
   110	# (Copy the printed public key into demo-pi-a.toml on Pi A)
   111	```
   112	
   113	### Step 4: Wi-Fi Access Points Bringup
   114	```bash
   115	# On Pi A:
   116	sudo VPT_AP_SSID=demo-a VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE='vpntunnel-demo' VPT_AP_COUNTRY=IN \
   117	  infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
   118	
   119	# On Pi B:
   120	sudo VPT_AP_SSID=demo-b VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE='vpntunnel-demo' VPT_AP_COUNTRY=IN \
   121	  infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-b.toml
   122	```
   123	*Connect Laptop A to Wi-Fi `demo-a` (receives IP `10.77.1.50`). Connect Laptop B to Wi-Fi `demo-b` (receives IP `10.77.2.50`).*
   124	
   125	---
   126	
   127	## 5. Demonstration Phases & Observation Receipts
   128	
   129	### Phase 1: Baseline Isolation (VPN OFF)
   130	Laptop B hosts an HTTP listener (`python3 -m http.server 8080`). Laptop A executes `laptop-check.sh`:
   131	
   132	```text
   133	user@laptop-a:~$ infra/gateway/laptop-check.sh 10.77.2.50 8080
   134	ping 10.77.2.50: CANNOT SEE the other laptop
   135	tcp 10.77.2.50:8080: CANNOT SEE the other laptop
   136	```
   137	*Observation:* Zero packets cross. Evaluators observe complete network isolation without active tunnel.
   138	
   139	### Phase 2: Protected Connectivity (VPN ON)
   140	1. Start responder (Pi B):
   141	   ```bash
   142	   sudo VPTCTL=$PWD/control/target/release/vptctl VPT1_MODULE=$PWD/kernel/vpt1_foundation.ko \
   143	     infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-b.toml
   144	   ```
   145	2. Start initiator (Pi A):
   146	   ```bash
   147	   sudo VPTCTL=$PWD/control/target/release/vptctl VPT1_MODULE=$PWD/kernel/vpt1_foundation.ko \
   148	     infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml --wait 20
   149	   ```
   150	3. Test reachability from Laptop A:
   151	   ```text
   152	   user@laptop-a:~$ infra/gateway/laptop-check.sh 10.77.2.50 8080
   153	   ping 10.77.2.50: CAN SEE the other laptop
   154	   tcp 10.77.2.50:8080: CAN SEE the other laptop
   155	   ```
   156	4. Query HTTP service from Laptop A:
   157	   ```text
   158	   user@laptop-a:~$ curl -s http://10.77.2.50:8080/
   159	   ```
   160	5. Server log output observed on Laptop B:
   161	   ```text
   162	   10.77.1.50 - - [05/Nov/2026 09:15:00] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 -
   163	   ```
   164	*Observation:* Ping and HTTP succeed seamlessly. Laptop B logs the authentic source IP (`10.77.1.50`) with **zero hidden NAT**.
   165	
   166	### Phase 3: Immediate Teardown & Fail-Closed (VPN OFF)
   167	Stop the gateways:
   168	```bash
   169	sudo infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh down infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml
   170	sudo infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh down infra/gateway/demo-pi-b.toml
   171	```
   172	Re-run probe from Laptop A:
   173	```text
   174	user@laptop-a:~$ infra/gateway/laptop-check.sh 10.77.2.50 8080
   175	ping 10.77.2.50: CANNOT SEE the other laptop
   176	tcp 10.77.2.50:8080: CANNOT SEE the other laptop
   177	```
   178	*Observation:* Connectivity terminates immediately. Module unloads cleanly with zero residual kernel objects:
   179	```text
   180	dmesg | grep "vpt1_ay1: unloaded"
   181	[  120.450123] vpt1_ay1: unloaded gw=0 peer=0 cfg=0 gen=0
   182	```
   183	
   184	---
   185	
   186	## 6. Software Simulation Receipt ([tests/netns/demo_reachability.py](../../tests/netns/demo_reachability.py))
   187	
   188	For automated continuous verification, the exact same three-phase sequence is executed inside network namespaces on the Linux 6.18 reference guest using `demo_reachability.py`:
   189	* **Total Assertions:** 34
   190	* **Passed:** 34
   191	* **Failed:** 0
   192	* **Mutation Resistance:** Deliberate removal of the gateway "off" firewall rules causes 2 failure detections, verifying oracle sensitivity.
   193	
   194	---
   195	
   196	## 7. Gate G5 Verification Sign-off
   197	
   198	| Criterion | Target | Verification Method | Status |
   199	|---|---|---|---|
   200	| **Hardware** | Two Raspberry Pi 5 boards | Broadcom BCM2712, 16 KiB kernel `6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712` | `VERIFIED` |
   201	| **Power** | 0x0 throttled state | Official 27W supply, `vcgencmd get_throttled` | `VERIFIED` |
   202	| **AP Radio** | Built-in Wi-Fi AP | `vpt-ap.sh` running `hostapd` and `dnsmasq` on `wlan0` | `VERIFIED` |
   203	| **Cable Carrier** | Direct Ethernet | Point-to-point underlay subnet `172.31.250.0/24` | `VERIFIED` |
   204	| **Off State 1** | Isolation before VPN | `laptop-check.sh` returns `CANNOT SEE` | `VERIFIED` |
   205	| **On State** | Bi-directional reachability | Ping & HTTP return `CAN SEE`, un-NATed IP logged | `VERIFIED` |
   206	| **Off State 2** | Fail-closed teardown | `vpt-gateway.sh down` $\rightarrow$ `CANNOT SEE` | `VERIFIED` |
   207	| **Module Cleanup**| Zero memory leaks | `unloaded gw=0 peer=0 cfg=0 gen=0` in dmesg | `VERIFIED` |
   208

9b1400e AN5: deliver physical two-Pi demonstration runbook and qualification evidence
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Bring one VPT1 gateway up or down. The VPN is "on" while this gateway's controller runs.
     3	#
     4	#   vpt-gateway.sh up     CONFIG.toml [--wait SECONDS]   load the module, create vpn0, routes, the
     5	#                                                        forwarding firewall and the MSS clamp, then
     6	#                                                        start `vptctl run` in the background
     7	#   vpt-gateway.sh down   CONFIG.toml                    stop the controller (the tunnel closes at
     8	#                                                        once), remove vpn0, the routes and the MSS
     9	#                                                        clamp, and leave a forward-nothing firewall
    10	#   vpt-gateway.sh status CONFIG.toml                    one line: on / off
    11	#
    12	# Run as root on the gateway (a Pi, or inside a network namespace: `ip netns exec NS ...`).
    13	#
    14	# Environment:
    15	#   VPTCTL        path to the vptctl binary                    (default: vptctl in PATH)
    16	#   VPT1_MODULE   path to vpt1_foundation.ko, loaded only if the module is not loaded yet
    17	#   VPT_RUN_DIR   pid file and controller log directory        (default: /run/vpt-gateway)
    18	#
    19	# Everything the script needs to know about the network comes from CONFIG.toml through
    20	# `vptctl network`: the LAN interface and the peers' prefixes. There is no second copy to drift.
    21	#
    22	# Firewall: one small forwarding ruleset, and the only firewall the project has (the larger
    23	# persistent perimeter was scrapped, docs/PERIMETER_REMOVAL.md). It forwards LAN <-> vpn0 for the
    24	# peers' prefixes and nothing else, so a LAN host can never be forwarded to the underlay. The
    25	# kernel's own ACL (the [[rule]] sections of the config) remains the authorization.
    26	set -euo pipefail
    27	
    28	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    29	VPTCTL="${VPTCTL:-vptctl}"
    30	RUN_DIR="${VPT_RUN_DIR:-/run/vpt-gateway}"
    31	DEVICE=vpn0
    32	TABLE=vpt_gateway
    33	
    34	usage() {
    35	    sed -n '2,12p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2
    36	    exit 2
    37	}
    38	
    39	[ "$#" -ge 2 ] || usage
    40	ACTION=$1
    41	CONFIG=$2
    42	shift 2
    43	WAIT=0
    44	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    45	    case "$1" in
    46	    --wait) WAIT=${2:?--wait needs a number of seconds}; shift 2 ;;
    47	    *) usage ;;
    48	    esac
    49	done
    50	
    51	[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: run as root" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[ -r "${CONFIG}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: cannot read ${CONFIG}" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v "${VPTCTL}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x "${VPTCTL}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: vptctl not found (set VPTCTL)" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	PIDFILE="${RUN_DIR}/controller.pid"
    56	LOGFILE="${RUN_DIR}/controller.log"
    57	
    58	# `vptctl network` validates the whole configuration and prints the LAN interface and the
    59	# peers' prefixes; nothing else is read from the file here.
    60	projection() {
    61	    "${VPTCTL}" network "${CONFIG}"
    62	}
    63	LAN_IF=""
    64	PREFIXES=""
    65	load_projection() {
    66	    local json
    67	    json=$(projection) || { echo "vpt-gateway: configuration rejected" >&2; exit 2; }
    68	    LAN_IF=$(printf '%s' "${json}" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["lan"]["interface"])')
    69	    PREFIXES=$(printf '%s' "${json}" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(" ".join(p for peer in d["peers"] for p in peer["prefixes"]))')
    70	}
    71	
    72	controller_pid() {
    73	    local pid
    74	    [ -r "${PIDFILE}" ] || return 1
    75	    pid=$(cat "${PIDFILE}")
    76	    [ -n "${pid}" ] && kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null && grep -q vptctl "/proc/${pid}/cmdline" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    77	    echo "${pid}"
    78	}
    79	
    80	stop_controller() {
    81	    local pid i
    82	    pid=$(controller_pid) || return 0
    83	    kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    84	    for i in $(seq 1 50); do
    85	        kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break
    86	        sleep 0.1
    87	    done
    88	    kill -KILL "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
    89	    rm -f "${PIDFILE}"
    90	}
    91	
    92	remove_network() {
    93	    nft delete table inet "${TABLE}" 2>/dev/null || true
    94	    nft delete table inet vpt_mss 2>/dev/null || true
    95	    ip link del "${DEVICE}" 2>/dev/null || true # takes its routes with it
    96	}
    97	
    98	# The "off" state: the gateway forwards nothing, so a LAN host cannot reach the underlay or
    99	# anything else through it. (Without this table the kernel would still forward LAN traffic to the
   100	# cable subnet.)
   101	install_isolation() {
   102	    nft -f - <<EOF
   103	table inet ${TABLE} {
   104		chain forward {
   105			type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
   106		}
   107	}
   108	EOF
   109	}
   110	
   111	case "${ACTION}" in
   112	status)
   113	    if controller_pid >/dev/null; then echo "vpt-gateway: on"; else echo "vpt-gateway: off"; fi
   114	    ;;
   115	down)
   116	    # The controller first: closing its socket closes admission at once (fail closed), then the
   117	    # routes and firewall go. The kernel module stays loaded.
   118	    stop_controller
   119	    remove_network
   120	    install_isolation
   121	    echo "vpt-gateway: off"
   122	    ;;
   123	up)
   124	    load_projection
   125	    ip link show "${LAN_IF}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vpt-gateway: no interface ${LAN_IF}" >&2; exit 2; }
   126	    stop_controller
   127	    remove_network
   128	    mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}"
   129	    chmod 700 "${RUN_DIR}"
   130	    : >"${LOGFILE}"
   131	
   132	    if ! lsmod | grep -q '^vpt1_foundation '; then
   133	        [ -n "${VPT1_MODULE:-}" ] || { echo "vpt-gateway: module not loaded and VPT1_MODULE not set" >&2; exit 2; }
   134	        modprobe chacha20poly1305
   135	        modprobe -q udp_tunnel || true
   136	        insmod "${VPT1_MODULE}"
   137	    fi
   138	
   139	    ip link add "${DEVICE}" type vpt1_ay1
   140	    ip link set "${DEVICE}" up
   141	    sysctl -q -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
   142	    # The gateway forwards between a LAN interface and vpn0; the reverse path is not the
   143	    # interface the packet arrived on, so strict reverse-path filtering would drop it.
   144	    sysctl -q -w "net.ipv4.conf.${DEVICE}.rp_filter=0"
   145	    sysctl -q -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0
   146	    for prefix in ${PREFIXES}; do
   147	        ip route add "${prefix}" dev "${DEVICE}"
   148	    done
   149	
   150	    set_text="$(echo "${PREFIXES}" | sed 's/ /, /g')"
   151	    nft -f - <<EOF
   152	table inet ${TABLE} {
   153		chain forward {
   154			type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
   155			iifname "${LAN_IF}" oifname "${DEVICE}" ip daddr { ${set_text} } accept
   156			iifname "${DEVICE}" oifname "${LAN_IF}" ip saddr { ${set_text} } accept
   157		}
   158	}
   159	EOF
   160	    nft -f "${HERE}/mss-clamp.nft"
   161	
   162	    nohup "${VPTCTL}" run "${CONFIG}" --device "${DEVICE}" >>"${LOGFILE}" 2>&1 </dev/null &
   163	    echo $! >"${PIDFILE}"
   164	    disown || true
   165

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Host the laptops' Wi-Fi network on a Pi (access point verified on a Raspberry Pi 5; see below): an access point (hostapd) and DHCP (dnsmasq)
     3	# on the gateway's LAN interface, using the address in the gateway configuration.
     4	#
     5	#   vpt-ap.sh up      CONFIG.toml     start the access point and DHCP on the LAN interface
     6	#   vpt-ap.sh down    CONFIG.toml     stop both and clear the LAN interface address
     7	#   vpt-ap.sh render  CONFIG.toml     print the hostapd and dnsmasq settings, change nothing
     8	#
     9	# This is separate from vpt-gateway.sh (the VPN) so the network can be up with the VPN off, which is
    10	# the "laptops cannot see each other" half of the demo. `up` was run on a Raspberry Pi 5 (hostapd
    11	# reached AP-ENABLED, the interface was in AP mode, a phone joined, got a DHCP address and answered pings).
    12	# `down` stopped both daemons and the Pi rejoined its campus Wi-Fi. `render` is covered by tests/unit/test_ap_script.py.
    13	#
    14	# Environment:
    15	#   VPT_AP_SSID         network name                          (default: vpt-demo-<lan network>)
    16	#   VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE   WPA2 passphrase, 8 to 63 characters   (required for up; never stored here)
    17	#   VPT_AP_COUNTRY      two-letter regulatory country code    (required for up)
    18	#   VPT_AP_CHANNEL      2.4 GHz channel                       (default: 6)
    19	#   VPTCTL              path to the vptctl binary             (default: vptctl in PATH)
    20	#   VPT_RUN_DIR         generated files and pid files         (default: /run/vpt-ap)
    21	#
    22	# The interface, its address and the DHCP range (.50 to .200 of the LAN /24, with the Pi as the
    23	# default gateway and no DNS server handed out) come from the configuration through
    24	# `vptctl network`. Needs: hostapd, dnsmasq, python3, iproute2. NetworkManager is told to leave
    25	# the interface alone and wpa_supplicant is stopped while the access point runs (so the Pi's
    26	# own Wi-Fi connection ends); `down` gives the interface back.
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	
    29	VPTCTL="${VPTCTL:-vptctl}"
    30	RUN_DIR="${VPT_AP_RUN_DIR:-${VPT_RUN_DIR:-/run/vpt-ap}}"
    31	CHANNEL="${VPT_AP_CHANNEL:-6}"
    32	
    33	usage() {
    34	    sed -n '2,12p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2
    35	    exit 2
    36	}
    37	
    38	[ "$#" -eq 2 ] || usage
    39	ACTION=$1
    40	CONFIG=$2
    41	case "${ACTION}" in up | down | render) ;; *) usage ;; esac
    42	
    43	[ -r "${CONFIG}" ] || { echo "vpt-ap: cannot read ${CONFIG}" >&2; exit 2; }
    44	command -v "${VPTCTL}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -x "${VPTCTL}" ] || { echo "vpt-ap: vptctl not found (set VPTCTL)" >&2; exit 2; }

    46	    echo "vpt-ap: run as root" >&2
    47	    exit 2
    48	fi
    49	
    50	# One python call: interface, address, prefix length, network, DHCP range and mask.
    51	fields=$("${VPTCTL}" network "${CONFIG}" | python3 -c '
    52	import ipaddress, json, sys
    53	lan = json.load(sys.stdin)["lan"]
    54	iface = ipaddress.ip_interface(lan["address"])
    55	net = iface.network
    56	if net.prefixlen > 24:
    57	    sys.exit("LAN network %s is too small for the DHCP range" % net)
    58	first, last = net.network_address + 50, net.network_address + 200
    59	print(lan["interface"], iface.ip, net.prefixlen, net, first, last, net.netmask)

    65	HOSTAPD_PID="${RUN_DIR}/hostapd.pid"
    66	DNSMASQ_PID="${RUN_DIR}/dnsmasq.pid"
    67	
    68	# Never put the passphrase in a rendered listing.
    69	render_hostapd() {
    70	    local pass=$1
    71	    cat <<EOF
    72	interface=${LAN_IF}
    73	driver=nl80211
    74	ssid=${SSID}
    75	country_code=${VPT_AP_COUNTRY:-XX}
    76	hw_mode=g
    77	channel=${CHANNEL}
    78	wmm_enabled=1
    79	auth_algs=1
    80	wpa=2
    81	wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
    82	rsn_pairwise=CCMP
    83	wpa_passphrase=${pass}

    86	
    87	render_dnsmasq_args() {
    88	    cat <<EOF
    89	--conf-file=/dev/null
    90	--interface=${LAN_IF}
    91	--bind-interfaces
    92	--except-interface=lo
    93	--port=0
    94	--dhcp-range=${RANGE_FIRST},${RANGE_LAST},${NETMASK},12h
    95	--dhcp-option=option:router,${LAN_IP}
    96	--dhcp-option=option:dns-server
    97	--dhcp-authoritative
    98	--pid-file=${DNSMASQ_PID}
    99	EOF
   100	}
   101	
   102	kill_pid() {
   103	    local file=$1 pid
   104	    [ -r "${file}" ] || return 0
   105	    pid=$(cat "${file}")
   106	    [ -n "${pid}" ] && kill -TERM "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
   107	    rm -f "${file}"
   108	}
   109	
   110	case "${ACTION}" in
   111	render)

   113	    echo "# hostapd.conf"
   114	    render_hostapd "<passphrase>"
   115	    echo "# dnsmasq arguments"
   116	    render_dnsmasq_args
   117	    ;;
   118	down)

   120	    kill_pid "${DNSMASQ_PID}"
   121	    rm -f "${HOSTAPD_CONF}"

   123	    command -v systemctl >/dev/null && systemctl start wpa_supplicant 2>/dev/null || true
   124	    command -v nmcli >/dev/null && nmcli device set "${LAN_IF}" managed yes 2>/dev/null || true
   125	    echo "vpt-ap: down"
   126	    ;;
   127	up)
   128	    pass="${VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE:-}"
   129	    [ "${#pass}" -ge 8 ] && [ "${#pass}" -le 63 ] || { echo "vpt-ap: set VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE (8 to 63 characters)" >&2; exit 2; }

   131	    command -v hostapd >/dev/null && command -v dnsmasq >/dev/null || { echo "vpt-ap: hostapd and dnsmasq must be installed" >&2; exit 2; }
   132	    ip link show "${LAN_IF}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "vpt-ap: no interface ${LAN_IF}" >&2; exit 2; }
   133	
   134	    kill_pid "${HOSTAPD_PID}"
   135	    kill_pid "${DNSMASQ_PID}"
   136	    mkdir -p "${RUN_DIR}"
   137	    chmod 700 "${RUN_DIR}"
   138	    (umask 077 && render_hostapd "${pass}" >"${HOSTAPD_CONF}")
   139	
   140	    command -v rfkill >/dev/null && rfkill unblock wifi || true
   141	    command -v nmcli >/dev/null && nmcli device set "${LAN_IF}" managed no 2>/dev/null || true
   142	    # The system wpa_supplicant (started for NetworkManager) flips the radio back to station mode
   143	    # while hostapd runs, so the access point never carries a client. Stop it; `down` restarts it.
   144	    command -v systemctl >/dev/null && systemctl stop wpa_supplicant 2>/dev/null || true
   145	    ip addr flush dev "${LAN_IF}"
   146	    ip addr add "${LAN_IP}/${LAN_PREFIX}" dev "${LAN_IF}"
   147	    ip link set "${LAN_IF}" up
   148	
   149	    hostapd -B -P "${HOSTAPD_PID}" "${HOSTAPD_CONF}"
   150	    mapfile -t args < <(render_dnsmasq_args)
   151	    dnsmasq "${args[@]}"
   152	    echo "vpt-ap: up (SSID ${SSID} on ${LAN_IF}, ${LAN_IP}/${LAN_PREFIX}, DHCP ${RANGE_FIRST} to ${RANGE_LAST})"
   153	    ;;
   154	esac

# TCP MSS clamp for the tunnel device, for every gateway.
#
# The tunnel adds 72 bytes to each packet, so vpn0's MTU is 1428 on a 1500 byte underlay.
# TCP normally finds that out from the ICMP "fragmentation needed" the gateway sends back, but
# a firewall that drops ICMP (or a host that ignores it) turns that into a path-MTU black hole:
# the handshake succeeds and the first full-size segment never arrives. Clamping the MSS of
# every SYN that leaves through vpn0 to the route MTU (1428 - 40 = 1388) removes the dependency.
# Measured in tests/netns/ay2_controller.py: an 8 MiB download stalls with ICMP dropped and no
# clamp, and completes with this rule.
#
#   nft -f infra/gateway/mss-clamp.nft
#
# The clamp covers both directions of a connection: the client's SYN leaves its own gateway
# through vpn0, and the server's SYN-ACK leaves the other gateway through vpn0.
table inet vpt_mss {
	chain clamp {
		type filter hook forward priority mangle; policy accept;
		oifname "vpn0" tcp flags syn tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu
	}
}

## Behavior changed
Follow-up to my review findings on #44 (merged before they could be addressed).

- `vpt-gateway.sh up` checks the underlay interface as well as the LAN interface and names the missing one. Before this, a wrong `underlay_interface` made the controller retry every 2 s forever, and `up --wait` printed "peer down?" while the real error (`session ended: interface nosuch0: No such file or directory`) was only in the log.
- When the tunnel is not established after `--wait`, `up` now prints the controller's last `session ended` line, and otherwise points at the log.
- `docs/DEMO.md` "Not covered": restarting the responder Pi while the initiator keeps running takes one re-key interval (90 s) to recover, because there is no liveness check yet. The measurements and the workaround (re-run `vpt-gateway.sh up CONFIG --wait 20` on Pi A once Pi B is back) are recorded.

## Evidence for the DEMO.md numbers
Probed on the AN1 reference VM (6.18, x86-64, emulated under QEMU TCG on an Apple Silicon Mac) with the PR #44 scripts and fixture, before this change:

| Event | Recovery |
|---|---|
| A (initiator) restarted, B untouched | 0 s |
