4:**Co-Owners / Hardware Leads:** Harsh (`HarshDhru23`), Aayush (`Aayush75`), Raj (`rajmodi8905`)  
(none above = absent)
     1	# Setting up the two Pis for the demo
     2	
     3	**Partly verified on one Pi** (`vpn-b`, Raspberry Pi 5, `6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712`, aarch64, 16 KiB pages, 4 November 2026). Verified there: the
     4	modules build natively with no warnings; the whole kernel test suite passes on it, including the controller, the zero-loss
     5	re-key test and the demo reachability test (both gateways in network namespaces on the one Pi); `vptctl` builds natively;
     6	the access point starts, a phone sees the network, joins it with the passphrase, gets a DHCP address (10.77.2.92) and answers
     7	pings from the Pi with no loss. **Not verified:** a laptop (rather than a phone) joining, two real Pis with the VPN between
     8	them, and Pi A. This is a checklist to work through, with the riskiest steps first. What the demo shows, and what is tested on the x86-64 reference VM, is in [DEMO.md](DEMO.md);
     9	the Pi 5 platform facts are in [PLATFORM_PI5.md](PLATFORM_PI5.md).
    10	
    11	Pi A uses `infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml` (laptop network 10.77.1.0/24, cable address 172.31.250.11) and Pi B
    12	uses `demo-pi-b.toml` (10.77.2.0/24, 172.31.250.12). Do steps 1 to 4 on each Pi while it still has internet; the
    13	demo itself needs none.
    14	
    15	## 1. Check the two risks first (about ten minutes each)
    16	
    17	- **Access-point mode.** `iw list` must show `AP` under "Supported interface modes" for the built-in radio (it does on `vpn-b`:
    18	  one AP plus one station at a time, on one channel). Then run `vpt-ap.sh up` (step 5) and join it from a laptop. The script
    19	  stops `wpa_supplicant` while the access point runs, because otherwise it switches the radio back to station mode; this ends
    20	  the Pi's own campus Wi-Fi connection, so manage the Pi over the cable.
    21	- **The module on this kernel.** Do step 3. The suite (`sudo VPT1_DISPOSABLE_VM=yes VPTCTL=... tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh`) loads, tests
    22	  and unloads it; it passed on `vpn-b`. The log shows `unloaded gw=0 peer=0 cfg=0 gen=0`.
    23	
    24	## 2. Packages
    25	
    26	Raspberry Pi OS 13 (trixie), 64-bit, kernel `6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712` with its headers installed.
    27	
    28	```sh
    29	sudo apt install build-essential nftables iproute2 hostapd dnsmasq python3 git iw
    30	sudo systemctl disable --now hostapd dnsmasq        # the script starts them itself
    31	sudo systemctl unmask hostapd
    32	```
    33	
    34	## 3. Build
    35	
    36	```sh
    37	git clone https://github.com/Aayush75/VPNTunnel && cd VPNTunnel
    38	make -C kernel                                       # release module: kernel/vpt1_foundation.ko
    39	curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh                  # then, in a new shell:
    40	cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path control/Cargo.toml   # control/target/release/vptctl
    41	```
    42	
    43	The `ring` crate needs a C compiler, so build `vptctl` on the Pi (it takes about a minute there), not by cross-compiling
    44	from a machine without a C toolchain.
    45	
    46	## 4. Identities and configuration
    47	
    48	```sh
    49	sudo install -d -m 700 /etc/vpntunnel
    50	sudo control/target/release/vptctl genkey --out /etc/vpntunnel/gw-a.key   # gw-b.key on Pi B; prints the public key
    51	```
    52	
    53	Copy the file for your Pi (`demo-pi-a.toml` or `-b`) and put the **other** Pi's public key in `public_key`. Check it
    54	with `vptctl check-config FILE --with-key`. Give the cable port its address (not persistent):
    55	
    56	```sh
    57	sudo ip addr add 172.31.250.11/24 dev eth0 && sudo ip link set eth0 up    # .12 on Pi B
    58	```
    59	
    60	## Facts found on `vpn-b`
    61	
    62	- **Power.** `vcgencmd get_throttled` showed `0x50000` (under-voltage and throttling have occurred) and the kernel logged
    63	  `Undervoltage detected!` several times. Use the official 27 W (5 V, 5 A) supply and a good cable, and check
    64	  `vcgencmd get_throttled` before a demo.
    65	- **Cable port.** Raspberry Pi OS gives up on a wired profile with no DHCP server and drops the address, so nothing answers on
    66	  the cable. Give `eth0` a fixed address (step 4); `nmcli con mod "Wired connection 1" ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses ...`.
    67	- **Packages.** `nftables`, `hostapd`, `dnsmasq`, `iw`, `git` were not installed. `sbin` tools (`iw`, `nft`) are not on a normal user's `PATH`.
    68	- **Smallest allocation** on this kernel is 64 bytes (`kmalloc-64`), unlike x86-64; a test that assumed small sizes failed until fixed.
    69	
    70	## 5. Run the demo
    71	
    72	On each Pi, as root (start Pi B first; it is the responder):
    73	
    74	```sh
    75	export VPTCTL=$PWD/control/target/release/vptctl VPT1_MODULE=$PWD/kernel/vpt1_foundation.ko
    76	VPT_AP_SSID=demo-a VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE='choose-one' VPT_AP_COUNTRY=IN infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh up FILE
    77	infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh up FILE --wait 20     # the VPN is on; `down` turns it off
    78	```
    79	
    80	Join each laptop to its Pi's network (it receives an address in 10.77.1.50 to 200, or 10.77.2.50 to 200). On a laptop:
    81	
    82	```sh
    83	infra/gateway/laptop-check.sh OTHER_LAPTOP_IP [TCP_PORT]      # CANNOT SEE with the VPN off, CAN SEE with it on
    84	```
    85	
    86	Run it with the VPN off, switch it on at both Pis, run it again, switch it off. Start something on the other laptop
    87	(for example `python3 -m http.server 8080`) to show a web page crossing. The VPN's state at each Pi is
    88	`vpt-gateway.sh status FILE`; its log is `/run/vpt-gateway/controller.log`.
    89	
    90	## If something fails
    91	
    92	- `dmesg | tail` on the Pi for the module; `controller.log` for the handshake (a Pi that is not reachable on the
    93	  cable never establishes). `ping 172.31.250.12` from Pi A tests the cable before the VPN is involved.
    94	- The tunnel costs 72 bytes per packet and `vpn0` has an MTU of 1428. Large UDP datagrams over 1400 bytes are
    95	  dropped by design; TCP and ping are fine ([AY2_DATAPATH.md](AY2_DATAPATH.md), "Packet size").
    96	- Keep `path_mtu = 1500` in the configuration; a smaller value drops packets silently ([DEMO.md](DEMO.md)).

second the controller reads the tunnel device's `/sys/class/net/vpn0/statistics` counters and asks the initiator for a new
exchange when either direction has carried 300 MiB or 300,000 records since the current keys were installed
(`src/usage.rs`). The counters are the device's, not one peer's, so with several peers one peer can be re-keyed a little
late; the gap to the hard limit absorbs it. Only the initiator can start an exchange; it sees the responder's traffic as its
received counters.

## Evidence (3 November 2026)

Guest `6.18.0-vpt1-ref` x86-64 (a long-lived working copy of the reference image, not the AN1 master).

- **Controller unit tests** (`cargo test --locked`, no kernel; 90 library tests pass): the state machine
  through an in-memory port (mirrored keys and locators, a lost INIT retransmitted with the same bytes, a
  lost RESPONSE answered from the cache with one generation installed, forged messages changing nothing,
  timeout and backoff, re-establishment with fresh keys, a stale kernel incarnation refreshed once), and
  the SNAPSHOT encoder, request builders and STATUS/event decoders against the exact record layouts.
- **`tests/netns/ay2_controller.py`, 21 assertions:** two `vptctl run` processes on the N1 fixture and
  nothing else configures anything. The tunnel comes up; ping and HTTP cross it with the original source;
  the underlay carries INIT, RESPONSE and RECORD datagrams and no private packet, no request ID and no
  static key in the clear; a denied port never arrives; the initiator re-keys every 8 s (test setting)
  and 2000 pings each way over 20 s, with 20 ms of delay on the underlay, lose nothing; a forged INIT is rejected and changes nothing; killing the
  controller stops traffic within 3 s (it releases the lease); restarting it brings the tunnel back.
  A mutation that swaps the key directions on the initiator only makes 7 assertions fail.
- Kernel: `EXCHANGE_TX` sends only a whole INIT (224 bytes, zero locator) or RESPONSE (176 bytes, nonzero
  locator) from the bound socket; a malformed one is `-EINVAL`, an unconfigured slot `-ENOENT`.
  `tests/netns/ay2_genl.py` covers these (71 assertions).

## Not covered

- No REKEY_START continuity grant, no activation handshake (CONFIRM/READY/COMMIT), and no liveness PING/PONG messages (a silent peer is noticed from the device counters instead, see above). INIT/RESPONSE are the only control messages that exist.
- One configuration revision per session; no live reconfiguration, no staged policy updates, and the
  controller does not install nftables or routes (`infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh` installs the forwarding ruleset; the `vpn0` device and
  routes are created by hand above).
- The kernel, not the controller, should allocate attempt IDs and receive locators per the design; this
  controller picks them (the kernel checks that locators are nonzero and unique in the gateway).
- No daemonization, privilege dropping or core-dump disabling, and no signal handler: stopping the process
  releases the socket, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.
- Not run: ARM64/Pi 5, macOS (the Linux-only modules are compiled out), long soak, many peers, concurrent
  reconfiguration against live traffic.

## Behavior changed
`vptctl run` can now change its configuration without a restart. It compares its file with the bytes it started from about once a second and applies a change as the next kernel revision in the same session (`VALIDATE`, `COMMIT_CONFIG` at N+1, lease renewed under N+1). Before this, one revision was committed per session and the only way to change a config was `vpt-gateway.sh down` then `up`.

- **The controller follows the kernel's classification, it does not repeat it.** After the commit it reads `STATUS`. A slot whose peer incarnation is unchanged keeps its exchange state and timers (the kernel keeps a peer only when `peer_cfg_equal` holds: role, path MTU, endpoint, key, prefixes). A replaced or new slot starts a fresh exchange at once; a removed slot is dropped with its cached RESPONSE (`Controller::reconfigure`).
- **Refusals leave everything as it was.** A parse or validation error, a different gateway key (that is a restart), a missing interface, or `-EINVAL`/`-ENOSPC`/`-EBUSY`/`-ENOMEM` from the kernel is logged once and not retried until the file changes. Errors that mean the session is gone (lost lease, wrong owner) still end it. The controller never lowers a rule count or rewrites a snapshot to fit. This is the behavior the #43 contract text asks for.
- The file is read bounded (64 KiB), compared by content (an editor's write-and-rename works; rewriting identical bytes is no change), and read once at session start so the validated bytes are the baseline.

In the #45 review I said I would replace the deleted `control/tests/perimeter.rs` cross-check with a permanent one. - COMMIT computes the shared TX MTU from all configured peer caps before activation/publication. RX retains its individual relationship cap. Manual MTU overrides are refused; Linux now supplies the local DF-set PTB on a real configured P1280 carrier.
- COMMIT acquires RTNL before retaining a gateway handler, avoiding a device-removal/reference-drain deadlock. Disruptive socket changes close old sessions before rebind; bind/MTU failure preserves cfg/staging, removes an uncommitted candidate listener and requires fresh peer incarnations on recovery.
- TX rechecks current policy/lease/incarnation/generation/size after crypto and routing, immediately before UDP output. Review draft for PR #64 (AN4 ledger). Comment only, not an approval.

What I did and did not do. I read docs/evidence/ACCEPTANCE_LEDGER.md at head 4d5e18d (the PR changes only that file and two lines of TEST_PLAN.md, and is based on main e0fd460), then opened the files each controller-related row cites on that tree. I checked every cited path against the tree, and I read the assertions in the cited scripts and Rust tests. I did not run any VM, kernel suite, netns script or cargo test, so "this test does not assert X" below means "I could not find the assertion in the source", not "I observed it failing". I only went through the rows that involve the controller or are shared with me (A10, A11, A15 to A18, A20, A24, A26, A29, A30, A33, A39, A40, A43, plus the sections that make claims about them). I did not audit the kernel-only and policy-only rows and say nothing about them either way.

Overall. The structure is what TEST_PLAN section 7 asks for, and several rows do have real evidence behind them. But the ledger marks all 43 rows PASS and the header says "COMPLETE (Gates G0-G4 Qualified)" (line 5, line 268). Several PASS rows cite files that do not exist, describe mechanisms the code does not have, or describe behaviour that exists only in open PRs. TEST_PLAN.md:232 says no row can be considered passed merely because it is listed, and TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:173 says not to mark tests complete because scripts exist. I think the ledger should carry a per-row status that distinguishes "asserted by a test on main", "partly asserted", "design intent only", and "only in open PR #N", rather than a flat PASS.

Cited files that do not exist at this head.
Line 37 (A10), line 44 (A17), line 66 (A39), line 216 (handshake attempt) and line 198 (pending exchanges) cite control/tests/handshake.rs or handshake.rs. There is no such file. The controller's integration tests are control/tests/exchange.rs, cacophony.rs, vpt1_independent.rs, genl_linux.rs and examples.rs; the state machine tests are inside control/src/session.rs. Line 80 says "In control/tests/handshake.rs, simulated packet loss tests verify bounded exponential backoff". No such test file exists on main.
Lines 40, 43, 64, 194, 199, 208 cite tests/unit/vpt1_gwtest.c or vpt1_gwtest.c. That is the module name; the source is tests/unit/vpt1_gateway_test.c (kernel/Makefile:25).
Line 67 (A40) and line 231 cite control/src/ for a handshake rate limiter. I found no token bucket in control/src. docs/CONTROLLER.md:46-48 says the kernel rate-limits INIT/RESPONSE delivery, and kernel/runtime/gateway.c:420 creates a per-peer exchange bucket at rate 1. I did not find the 4/s per-gateway bucket or any test that floods it.
Lines 51 and 67 cite "control/tests/" and "control/src/" as directories, which is not a test reference.
Many bare names in the table (ay2_datapath.py, hr4_ip.py, independent_ik_vector.py and so on) resolve to tests/netns/ or tools/ and are fine, but a row should give the full path so a reader can open it.

Row by row, controller and shared rows.

A10 (line 37, Raj). Evidence exists, under different names. control/tests/exchange.rs:135 (responder_rejects_unpinned_initiator), :146 (responder_identity_check_after_matching_prologue), :174 (initiator_rejects_wrong_responder), :196 and :206 (all-zero DH), and :273 (tampering) assert that respond() or finish() returns an error, so no SessionKeys value is produced. control/src/session.rs:748 asserts a forged RESPONSE or garbage INIT installs nothing and is counted as rejected. tools/independent_ik_vector.py is a vector generator that feeds control/tests/vectors/vpt1-ik-independent.json, which control/tests/vpt1_independent.rs reads; it is not itself a test. Missing: nothing material for the controller half. Fix the file names. The ledger's "unauthorized static key ... no session keys generated" is correct as a Result type property, not as a counter.

A11 (line 38). tests/netns/ay2_datapath.py:329-334 asserts RX_REPLAY, RX_AUTH_FAIL, RX_UNKNOWN_LOCATOR, RX_BAD_SOURCE, RX_MALFORMED and that nothing was delivered. The ledger names a counter "rx_crypto_err"; the counter is RX_AUTH_FAIL. This test keys the gateways directly over Netlink, so it does not exercise the controller; that is fine for A11 but the "Raj" co-ownership is nominal.

A15 (line 42, Raj + Aayush). This one holds up best. tests/netns/ay2_controller.py:331-347 adds 20 ms netem delay to both underlay links, re-keys every 8 s and asserts zero loss over 2000 pings each way. tests/netns/ay4_soak.py:118-122 asserts zero loss both ways, intact downloads and continuing re-keys. The ledger cites ay4_usage_rekey.py and ay4_soak.py but not ay2_controller.py, which is where the netem assertion lives. Corrections: the controller re-keys 90 s after success (control/src/session.rs:52), not at the kernel's 120 s soft age as line 218 says; and the switch to the new generation happens on the first authenticated record or after 2 s, whichever is first (docs/AY4_REKEY.md:25-27). docs/AY4_REKEY.md "Not covered" and docs/CONTROLLER.md:89 say there is no activation handshake (CONFIRM/READY/COMMIT) and no continuity grant. DESIGN_PLAN.md A15 asks for "confirmed replacement". The ledger should state that the confirmed-replacement part is not implemented, or record an approved scope change.

A16 (line 43). The kernel unit test touches hard-age replacement (tests/unit/vpt1_gateway_test.c:677, :816, :990). tests/netns/ay4_silence.py does not do what the row says: it kills and restarts the responder's controller (lines 88-100) and checks recovery in seconds. I found no netns test that prevents re-key completion until hard expiry and asserts forwarding stops. "Expired key material is zeroed" I could not find asserted anywhere I looked.

A17 (line 44). DESIGN_PLAN.md says "inject pre-restart records; old traffic rejected". I found no test that does that. What exists: tests/netns/ay4_silence.py restarts the responder and asserts recovery with new keys; tests/netns/ay2_genl.py:297-302 asserts a stale incarnation is refused at STAGE_GENERATION; control/src/session.rs:847 asserts a stale kernel incarnation is refreshed once. tests/netns/ay5_runtime.py is cited but does not look at incarnations. "Controller incarnation" in the row is wrong: the 16-byte incarnation is the kernel's per-peer value. Status should be partial.

A18 (line 45). tests/netns/ay5_runtime.py:184-205 does SIGKILL the controller at random moments and asserts the tunnel comes back and no download arrives corrupted. tests/netns/ay4_silence.py:92 asserts traffic stops within 15 s after a SIGKILL of the responder's controller. Not asserted anywhere I found: that closure happens within the 5 s lease bound (the loosest check is 15 s; ay2_controller.py:358 uses a graceful SIGTERM via Controller.stop(), lines 121-127 of that file), that the kernel "tears down crypto sessions", or the "frees unreferenced memory" part except indirectly through the unload report in tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh:129-135.

A20 (line 47, Raj + Aayush + Harsh). The ledger says stale commits are rejected with -EBUSY. In tests/netns/ay2_genl.py a stale revision gives ESTALE (lines 224-225 and 257-259) and a COMMIT with the wrong revision gives ENOENT (248-249); -EBUSY is the retired-snapshot ceiling, a different thing. The controller half of A20 (an invalid or partial update leaves the previous policy, a delayed completion from a superseded revision cannot reactivate) cannot exist on main: docs/CONTROLLER.md "Not covered" says one revision per session and no staged policy updates, and TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:5 and :53 say RJ4 is not done. That work is in my open PR #54 (reload) and #55 (differential check against VALIDATE), neither merged. The row should say so rather than PASS.

A24 (line 51, Raj + Anvit). The row says "under artificial packet loss, ... exponential backoff ... restores session when carrier heals". There is no packet-loss injection anywhere in the tree: the only netem command is `delay 20ms` (ay2_controller.py:331). ay4_silence.py is a restart test, not an impairment test. The backoff and retry bounds are asserted only in a fake-clock unit test, control/src/session.rs:788 (an_attempt_that_never_completes_backs_off_and_retries), with a fake wire that drops packets. DESIGN_PLAN.md A24 asks to lose, reorder and delay outer packets and block the path. Loss, reorder and a blocked path are not covered by any netns test. My open PR #52 adds 27 portable adversarial tests for the bounds, but no Linux impairment test exists. Section 3.1 (lines 76-80) is worse than the row: it says netem delay is injected in ay4_usage_rekey.py and ay4_soak.py (the grep finds netem only in ay2_controller.py), says "delay, loss, reordering, and jitter" (only delay), and says ay4_silence.py injects "complete one-way and two-way carrier loss" (it does not).

A26 (line 53, All). The row cites tests/netns/ay5_runtime.py and n2_fixture.sh. ay5_runtime.py builds the N1 fixture (line 87), which has one gateway pair, so there is no peer C whose latency could be measured. I searched the tree: n2_fixture.sh is referenced only by ci-gate.yml, which runs its setup and check, not any traffic test. The same applies to the N2 claims in A14, A25, A27, A36 and A41 (lines 41, 52, 54, 63, 68); I did not check their policy-level evidence, only the N2 usage. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md "Not covered" itself says "One peer pair".

A29 (line 56). Substantially backed by ay5_runtime.py:141-150: the check is controller CPU under 0.5 s, not "under 0.02 s"; docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md reports 0.01 s measured. Cite the actual threshold.

A30 (line 57, All). The allocation-failure injection is real in the gateway code only. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md "Not covered" says acl.c and generation.c failures are not injected and that queue-limit overload was not tested with a new test. N3 flood and queue exhaustion are not shown for the controller or for the kernel queues by anything cited.

A33 (line 60). ay5_runtime.py runs ROUNDS=4 by default (line 32). Four rounds of start, stop, kill and delete is useful but is not the "rapid sequential loops" the row describes, and it is one peer pair.

A39 (line 66, Raj + Aayush). The config half is real: control/src/config.rs:597 (rejects_duplicate_identity_and_endpoint) accepts A and C distinct identities and rejects a duplicated pinned key. The runtime half is not: no test brings up a gateway B with two peers and shows two pairwise exchanges with independent keys. control/examples/gw-b-n2.toml exists but nothing runs it; the controller session tests in session.rs use a single peer slot. docs/CONTROLLER.md "Not covered" lists "many peers" as not run.

A40 (line 67, Raj + Aayush). The row, section 7.2 line 223 and the invariants table say "PING every 5 s, 15 s deadline, 3 missed PINGs". On main there are no PING/PONG messages at all (docs/CONTROLLER.md:89). What exists is a counter-based check in control/src/usage.rs:112-116 (6 s of sending with no answer, at least 5 records sent, 15 s cooldown), tested by tests/netns/ay4_silence.py as a responder restart. The 5 s / 15 s kernel liveness is Aayush's open PR #63 (stacked on #61). The design's A40 also asks for a responder-side soft or hard key limit and a single failed underlay direction; control/src/session.rs:857 shows the responder never initiates, and I found no one-direction-failure test on main (#63 adds one, ay4_liveness.py).

A43 (line 70, Raj + Aayush + Anvit). The row cites docs/CONTROLLER.md for an "operational policy enforces clean lease expiration and fresh key negotiation". docs/CONTROLLER.md contains no statement about suspend, snapshot or VM restore (I searched the docs; only the planning documents mention it). TEST_PLAN.md:320 does say the default profile excludes live suspend, snapshot and clone and that it should be prevented operationally, and line 278 allows "tested explicit unsupported transition policy". So the exclusion is legitimate, but a PASS needs the operator-facing statement to exist somewhere a reader of the runbook will see, and ideally one test. My open PR #51 (suspend-safe timers) is related and is not merged.

Other sections.
Mutation table (lines 115-132). I recognise most rows as results already recorded in the component documents (AY2_DATAPATH.md:93, AY5_RUNTIME.md:21, HR5.md:140, DEMO.md:78, CONTROLLER.md:82), not mutations AN4 ran. That is fine, but say "recorded in" with a link, and do not claim "zero false-positive passes" (line 134), which no document I read establishes.
Section 7.2 line 218 and 219: soft and hard age are kernel values (vpt1_generation.h:9-10); the controller starts at 90 s. Line 222 mixes 15 s and 10 s for the retiring overlap; the code is 10 s (vpt1_gateway.h:30).
Section 9 gate table (lines 253-262). TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:148 requires for G3 that all applicable A01-A43 pass, and for G4 a frozen commit, sanitizer runs, repeated lifecycle tests and a reproduction by another developer. ci-gate.yml runs the N0 baseline and the N2 fixture check only (lines 56-68); the kernel suite is not in CI (TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:165 says the privileged lanes are missing). docs/QUALITY_CHECKS.md and docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md both say KCSAN, hours-long runs, several peers and the Pi were not covered for those results. G3 and G4 "PASSED" overstates that.
Section 8 line 248: "Complete suite PASS" for the Pi cites PI_SETUP.md, which says one Pi (vpn-b) passed the suite with both gateways as namespaces and that Pi A and two real Pis are not verified. Line 249 puts KASAN and kmemleak under the x86 column and "clean module unload" under the Pi column, which is accurate only if read that way.
Row A32 (line 59, I18). It cites two documents, not a benchmark. There is no tests/benchmark directory, and TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:73 asks for a separate benchmark fixture. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md reports a 48 MiB transfer taking about 5 s as an AY5 observation, not a fair measurement.
R12 (line 157) is marked VERIFIED on the strength of "non-author reviews". This PR has none yet.

What would make this mergeable in my view. Replace PASS with a status per row and a column that names the exact file and line or assertion, with an explicit "only in open PR #N" marker where that is the case; fix the file names above; remove the claims about loss, reorder and jitter netem, 15 s PING liveness, handshake.rs and a controller token bucket unless they land first; change the header and gate table to what has actually run. I think the honest version of this document is still valuable: it would show roughly which rows have an assertion, and which need work. In my own rows I am taking the follow-ups for A17, A18, A20, A24, A39, A40 and A43.

Comment only, not an approval. Nothing here was run.

Not asserted anywhere I found: that closure happens within the 5 s lease bound (the loosest check is 15 s; ay2_controller.py:358 uses a graceful SIGTERM via Controller.stop(), lines 121-127 of that file), that the kernel "tears down crypto sessions", or the "frees unreferenced memory" part except indirectly through the unload report in tools/kernel_vm_suite.sh:129-135.

A20 (line 47, Raj + Aayush + Harsh). The ledger says stale commits are rejected with -EBUSY. In tests/netns/ay2_genl.py a stale revision gives ESTALE (lines 224-225 and 257-259) and a COMMIT with the wrong revision gives ENOENT (248-249); -EBUSY is the retired-snapshot ceiling, a different thing. The controller half of A20 (an invalid or partial update leaves the previous policy, a delayed completion from a superseded revision cannot reactivate) cannot exist on main: docs/CONTROLLER.md "Not covered" says one revision per session and no staged policy updates, and TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:5 and :53 say RJ4 is not done. That work is in my open PR #54 (reload) and #55 (differential check against VALIDATE), neither merged. The row should say so rather than PASS.

A24 (line 51, Raj + Anvit). The row says "under artificial packet loss, ... exponential backoff ... restores session when carrier heals". There is no packet-loss injection anywhere in the tree: the only netem command is `delay 20ms` (ay2_controller.py:331). ay4_silence.py is a restart test, not an impairment test. The backoff and retry bounds are asserted only in a fake-clock unit test, control/src/session.rs:788 (an_attempt_that_never_completes_backs_off_and_retries), with a fake wire that drops packets. DESIGN_PLAN.md A24 asks to lose, reorder and delay outer packets and block the path. Loss, reorder and a blocked path are not covered by any netns test. My open PR #52 adds 27 portable adversarial tests for the bounds, but no Linux impairment test exists. Section 3.1 (lines 76-80) is worse than the row: it says netem delay is injected in ay4_usage_rekey.py and ay4_soak.py (the grep finds netem only in ay2_controller.py), says "delay, loss, reordering, and jitter" (only delay), and says ay4_silence.py injects "complete one-way and two-way carrier loss" (it does not).

A26 (line 53, All). The row cites tests/netns/ay5_runtime.py and n2_fixture.sh. ay5_runtime.py builds the N1 fixture (line 87), which has one gateway pair, so there is no peer C whose latency could be measured. I searched the tree: n2_fixture.sh is referenced only by ci-gate.yml, which runs its setup and check, not any traffic test. The same applies to the N2 claims in A14, A25, A27, A36 and A41 (lines 41, 52, 54, 63, 68); I did not check their policy-level evidence, only the N2 usage. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md "Not covered" itself says "One peer pair".

A29 (line 56). Substantially backed by ay5_runtime.py:141-150: the check is controller CPU under 0.5 s, not "under 0.02 s"; docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md reports 0.01 s measured. Cite the actual threshold.

A30 (line 57, All). The allocation-failure injection is real in the gateway code only. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md "Not covered" says acl.c and generation.c failures are not injected and that queue-limit overload was not tested with a new test. N3 flood and queue exhaustion are not shown for the controller or for the kernel queues by anything cited.

A33 (line 60). ay5_runtime.py runs ROUNDS=4 by default (line 32). Four rounds of start, stop, kill and delete is useful but is not the "rapid sequential loops" the row describes, and it is one peer pair.

A39 (line 66, Raj + Aayush). The config half is real: control/src/config.rs:597 (rejects_duplicate_identity_and_endpoint) accepts A and C distinct identities and rejects a duplicated pinned key. The runtime half is not: no test brings up a gateway B with two peers and shows two pairwise exchanges with independent keys. control/examples/gw-b-n2.toml exists but nothing runs it; the controller session tests in session.rs use a single peer slot. docs/CONTROLLER.md "Not covered" lists "many peers" as not run.

A40 (line 67, Raj + Aayush). The row, section 7.2 line 223 and the invariants table say "PING every 5 s, 15 s deadline, 3 missed PINGs". On main there are no PING/PONG messages at all (docs/CONTROLLER.md:89). What exists is a counter-based check in control/src/usage.rs:112-116 (6 s of sending with no answer, at least 5 records sent, 15 s cooldown), tested by tests/netns/ay4_silence.py as a responder restart. The 5 s / 15 s kernel liveness is Aayush's open PR #63 (stacked on #61). The design's A40 also asks for a responder-side soft or hard key limit and a single failed underlay direction; control/src/session.rs:857 shows the responder never initiates, and I found no one-direction-failure test on main (#63 adds one, ay4_liveness.py).

A43 (line 70, Raj + Aayush + Anvit). The row cites docs/CONTROLLER.md for an "operational policy enforces clean lease expiration and fresh key negotiation". docs/CONTROLLER.md contains no statement about suspend, snapshot or VM restore (I searched the docs; only the planning documents mention it). TEST_PLAN.md:320 does say the default profile excludes live suspend, snapshot and clone and that it should be prevented operationally, and line 278 allows "tested explicit unsupported transition policy". So the exclusion is legitimate, but a PASS needs the operator-facing statement to exist somewhere a reader of the runbook will see, and ideally one test. My open PR #51 (suspend-safe timers) is related and is not merged.

Other sections.
Mutation table (lines 115-132). I recognise most rows as results already recorded in the component documents (AY2_DATAPATH.md:93, AY5_RUNTIME.md:21, HR5.md:140, DEMO.md:78, CONTROLLER.md:82), not mutations AN4 ran. That is fine, but say "recorded in" with a link, and do not claim "zero false-positive passes" (line 134), which no document I read establishes.
Section 7.2 line 218 and 219: soft and hard age are kernel values (vpt1_generation.h:9-10); the controller starts at 90 s. Line 222 mixes 15 s and 10 s for the retiring overlap; the code is 10 s (vpt1_gateway.h:30).
Section 9 gate table (lines 253-262). TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:148 requires for G3 that all applicable A01-A43 pass, and for G4 a frozen commit, sanitizer runs, repeated lifecycle tests and a reproduction by another developer. ci-gate.yml runs the N0 baseline and the N2 fixture check only (lines 56-68); the kernel suite is not in CI (TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:165 says the privileged lanes are missing). docs/QUALITY_CHECKS.md and docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md both say KCSAN, hours-long runs, several peers and the Pi were not covered for those results. G3 and G4 "PASSED" overstates that.
Section 8 line 248: "Complete suite PASS" for the Pi cites PI_SETUP.md, which says one Pi (vpn-b) passed the suite with both gateways as namespaces and that Pi A and two real Pis are not verified. Line 249 puts KASAN and kmemleak under the x86 column and "clean module unload" under the Pi column, which is accurate only if read that way.
Row A32 (line 59, I18). It cites two documents, not a benchmark. There is no tests/benchmark directory, and TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:73 asks for a separate benchmark fixture. docs/AY5_RUNTIME.md reports a 48 MiB transfer taking about 5 s as an AY5 observation, not a fair measurement.
R12 (line 157) is marked VERIFIED on the strength of "non-author reviews". This PR has none yet.

What would make this mergeable in my view. Replace PASS with a status per row and a column that names the exact file and line or assertion, with an explicit "only in open PR #N" marker where that is the case; fix the file names above; remove the claims about loss, reorder and jitter netem, 15 s PING liveness, handshake.rs and a controller token bucket unless they land first; change the header and gate table to what has actually run. I think the honest version of this document is still valuable: it would show roughly which rows have an assertion, and which need work. In my own rows I am taking the follow-ups for A17, A18, A20, A24, A39, A40 and A43.

Comment only, not an approval. Nothing here was run.

input.content:
Review draft for PR #65 (AN5 runbook and evidence). Comment only, not an approval.

What I did and did not do. I read docs/evidence/AN5_DEMO.md and the two-line change to docs/DEMO.md at head 9b1400e (based on main e0fd460), and compared the runbook step by step with infra/gateway/vpt-gateway.sh, infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh, infra/gateway/laptop-check.sh, infra/gateway/demo-pi-a.toml and demo-pi-b.toml, infra/gateway/mss-clamp.nft, control/src/main.rs, docs/DEMO.md, docs/PI_SETUP.md and docs/PLATFORM_PI5.md. I also compared with my open PR #53. This is a static read. I did not run any script, VM or Pi, so statements that a step "would fail" are conclusions from reading the code, and I say which.

The main problem: the receipts are not backed by a run. AN5_DEMO.md:5 says "QUALIFIED & READY FOR LIVE LAB EVALUATION (Gate G5)", lines 27-41 give a hardware inventory with "Rev 1.0 (8GB)", an official 27 W supply and "vcgencmd get_throttled = 0x0", lines 160-163 and 179-181 show log and dmesg output with timestamps, and lines 196-207 mark every row of the G5 table VERIFIED. The repository says otherwise in several places. docs/DEMO.md:90 (unchanged by this PR) says two real Pis with the VPN between them have not been run. docs/PI_SETUP.md:3-8 says only one Pi (vpn-b) was exercised, with both gateways as namespaces, and that a laptop joining, two real Pis and Pi A are not verified. docs/PLATFORM_PI5.md:16 records Rev 1.1, line 26 records get_throttled 0x50000 with undervoltage warnings, and lines 123 and 186 say Pi A is untested and power remediation is pending. TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:5 says Pi A and the two-Pi demo have not run. The PR adds no manifest, log, capture or JSON file, only the two documents, whereas TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:73 lists both Pi manifests, power and radio qualification, retained failures and a frozen-commit physical test as AN5's required evidence. The sample dmesg line and server log are indistinguishable from observed output. If these were not observed on two real Pis, they should not appear as receipts; the same text could be kept as an expected-output template with blanks to fill in during the live run. The DEMO.md change (line 49) also deletes "(untested)" from the PI_SETUP reference, which contradicts DEMO.md:90 in the same file. I would keep "(untested)", retitle AN5_DEMO.md as a runbook, set the status to "not yet run on hardware", and turn the G5 table into an empty checklist.

Steps that would not work as written (from reading the scripts).

AN5_DEMO.md:114-121 (Step 4). vpt-ap.sh needs vptctl: infra/gateway/vpt-ap.sh:44 exits 2 with "vptctl not found (set VPTCTL)" unless VPTCTL is set or vptctl is on PATH. The runbook sets only VPT_AP_SSID, VPT_AP_PASSPHRASE and VPT_AP_COUNTRY. Step 3 calls the binary by path (control/target/release/vptctl), so it is not on PATH. PI_SETUP.md:75 exports VPTCTL before running the access point script; the runbook does not. This step should fail on a fresh Pi.

AN5_DEMO.md:178-181 (Phase 3). The text says the module "unloads cleanly" after `down` and shows `vpt1_ay1: unloaded`. vpt-gateway.sh `down` (lines 115-122, comment at 116-117) stops the controller, removes vpn0, routes and the clamp, installs the forward-nothing table, and leaves the module loaded. That unload line is logged only by an rmmod, which the runbook never runs. Either add `rmmod vpt1_foundation` or remove the claim.

AN5_DEMO.md:69-86 (Step 1). Three gaps against docs/PI_SETUP.md. There is no kernel header package, and PI_SETUP.md:26 requires the headers for 6.18.34+rpt-rpi-2712 for `make -C kernel`. There is no Rust install: apt gives no rustup, the repo pins a toolchain (control/rust-toolchain.toml), and PI_SETUP.md:39 runs the rustup installer before `cargo build`. There is no clone: line 83 does `cd /home/anvit/VPNTunnel`, which is one person's home directory, not a path on the other Pi. The cargo and make lines would fail on a clean Pi as written.

AN5_DEMO.md:88-98 (Step 2). `ip addr add` on eth0 is not persistent, and PI_SETUP.md:65-66 records that Raspberry Pi OS drops a wired address when no DHCP server answers; PI_SETUP gives an nmcli fix. The runbook has no such fix, and the later ping check at line 97 can pass and then stop passing before the tunnel is started. The kernel binds its UDP socket on the underlay address at commit (see docs/CONTROLLER.md step 3), so a lost address surfaces as a controller that cannot start.

AN5_DEMO.md:100-111 (Step 3). PI_SETUP.md:53-54 tells the operator to run `vptctl check-config FILE --with-key` after putting in the peer key. The runbook skips it. The checked-in demo-pi-*.toml carry the sample public keys from control/examples, and a wrong key otherwise appears only in controller.log. With my PR #53 the `--wait` timeout prints the last session error, but that is not merged. Also, editing the tracked demo-pi-*.toml dirties the tree, which sits badly with a "frozen commit" requirement (TEAM_WORK_PLAN.md:149); PI_SETUP.md:53 says to copy the file for the Pi, which is the better instruction.

AN5_DEMO.md:129-137 (Phase 1). The "VPN off" table is only installed by `vpt-gateway.sh` itself: `install_isolation` runs from `down` (vpt-gateway.sh:101-109 and 118-122), and `up` installs the working table. On a Pi that has only run vpt-ap.sh, no forward-nothing table exists, so the "CANNOT SEE" baseline rests on there being no route to the other subnet and on ip_forward being 0. I think that is probably fine on a fresh Pi OS, but I did not test it, and a stale ip_forward=1 from an earlier `up` followed by a manual `ip link del` would change the result. The runbook could run `vpt-gateway.sh down CONFIG` on both Pis first, so the baseline is the fail-closed state the demo is meant to show. This is the same state tests/netns/demo_reachability.py checks.

Management access. vpt-ap.sh:142-144 stops wpa_supplicant while the access point runs, which ends the Pi's own Wi-Fi connection. The runbook does not say how the operator reaches each Pi afterwards. PI_SETUP.md:20 says manage it over the cable (but the cable carries only the static 172.31.250.x demo addresses), and DEMO.md:88-89 says to join the Pi's own Wi-Fi and use SSH to 10.77.1.1 or 10.77.2.1. Say one of these.

Small points. AN5_DEMO.md:22 and 123 state that laptops get 10.77.1.50 and 10.77.2.50; the DHCP pool starts at .50 (vpt-ap.sh:58), so that is only the first lease, and the sample log at line 162 hard-codes it. Line 63's clamp of 1388 is right (mss-clamp.nft, 1428 minus 40). The hardware row says the radio is in AP mode on both Pis, but only Pi B's radio has been shown to host an AP (PLATFORM_PI5.md:123).

Responder restart outage (#53) consistency. AN5_DEMO.md says nothing about restarting one Pi while the other runs; the words restart, outage and 90 do not appear in it. DEMO.md in this PR does not touch the "Not covered" section either. My PR #53 adds a paragraph there saying a restarted responder takes 90 s to recover because there is no liveness check yet. That paragraph is now stale against main: after #53 branched, main gained commit 7d58ec2, which makes the controller re-key when the peer goes silent (control/src/usage.rs:112-116, docs/CONTROLLER.md:50-57, tests/netns/ay4_silence.py). The recorded recovery there is about 7.6 s after the responder's controller is killed and restarted, provided the initiator has traffic of its own to send (at least 5 records in 6 s) and with a 15 s cooldown; an idle initiator still waits for the 90 s age timer. So the number to state in the demo documents is "a few seconds with laptop traffic running, up to 90 s if Pi A is idle", and I will correct #53 to say that and cite ay4_silence.py. The workaround in #53 (run `vpt-gateway.sh up CONFIG --wait 20` on Pi A once Pi B is back) still works as a manual restart and should also go in the AN5 runbook, in the live-demo section. If the kernel liveness in open PR #63 lands, the figure changes again (a 15 s closure and recovery by re-key), so the two documents should link to one place for that number rather than each repeating it.

What I checked and found consistent. The command forms match the code: `vptctl genkey --out`, `check-config FILE --with-key`, `network FILE` and `run FILE --device` exist (control/src/main.rs:20-65). `vpt-gateway.sh up CONFIG --wait 20` parses (vpt-gateway.sh:44-49), `down CONFIG` and `status CONFIG` exist, and VPTCTL and VPT1_MODULE are the variables it reads. Starting Pi B before Pi A matches DEMO.md:26. The policy description in section 3.2 matches the six whole-network rules in demo-pi-a.toml. The 34-assertion figure in section 6 matches DEMO.md:68, and that run was in namespaces on the x86 reference VM, not on Pis, which section 6 does say.

Comment only, not an approval. Nothing here was run, and I have not seen any physical-hardware output.

content.text:
Both drafts are written and nothing was posted to GitHub. I ran no VMs and no tests, so every finding below comes from reading the source. I fetched the PR heads (#64 at 4d5e18d, #65 at 9b1400e) and left your worktree on `raj/validate-differential` (I only checked out detached heads to read).
